# dsh-ga-browser-bridge

Control your **real Chrome** (with all your login sessions intact) from
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) —
directly over the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

**No GenericAgent. No Python. No browser extension.** Just a DSH plugin that
talks CDP to the Chrome you already use.

> This plugin replaces the legacy `ga-browser-bridge` MCP bridge
> (`br_mcp.py` + GA master + `tmwd_cdp_bridge` extension). The five
> `browser_*` tools keep the **same names, same parameters, same return
> shapes**, so existing prompts and agent memories keep working.
>
> **Acknowledgment**: the design, the tool semantics, and the original
> real-browser-bridge concept come from the **GA (GenericAgent) project** —
> its `TMWebDriver` / `tmwd_cdp_bridge` extension / `br_mcp.py` bridge proved
> the approach and defined the `browser_*` tool contract this plugin keeps
> byte-compatible. Thanks to the GA project for the foundation.

> **中文文档**: [README.zh.md](./README.zh.md)

---


### Why

The old bridge chained four layers:

```
DSH ──MCP(stdio)──> br_mcp.py ──HTTP──> GA master :18766 ──WS──> extension ──CDP──> Chrome
```

Any broken layer killed the whole chain, and it required the GA desktop app,
a bundled Python runtime, and a manually loaded Chrome extension.

This plugin removes all three dependencies:

```
DSH ──native tools──> plugin ──CDP (WebSocket)──> Chrome (--remote-debugging-port=9222)
```

### Features

- Five tools: `browser_tabs`, `browser_scan`, `browser_execute_js`,
  `browser_cdp`, `browser_cookies`
- **Two transports, one tool contract:**
  - **Extension transport** — drives the Chrome you *already have open*, with
    your existing logins, no restart, and unaffected by the Chrome 136+
    default-profile restriction. Requires installing the bundled extension
    once → [docs/EXTENSION.md](docs/EXTENSION.md)
  - **CDP debug-port transport** — no extra install; works headless and on
    servers; needs a separate profile on Chrome 136+
- Reuses your **default Chrome profile** — everything you are already logged
  into keeps working (extension transport), or a copied profile (CDP transport)
- Auto-launches Chrome with the debug port when it is closed (CDP transport)
- Raw CDP passthrough (`browser_cdp`) for screenshots, trusted input, file
  upload, cross-origin iframes, shadow DOM
- Batch CDP commands with `$N.path` references to prior results
- TypeScript, ESM, single runtime dependency (`ws`)

### Which transport should I use?

| You want… | Use |
|---|---|
| To drive the browser you are already using, logged in as you | **Extension** |
| No install step, headless/CI/servers | **CDP debug port** |
| Both (try extension, fall back) | `transport: auto` (default) |

The extension transport is the answer to "why can't it just attach to my open
Chrome?" — [docs/EXTENSION.md](docs/EXTENSION.md) explains the install, the
yellow "started debugging" bar you will see, and the limitations.

> **Status**: the extension transport is new. Its automated tests are green
> (130/130 including the bridge over a real loopback socket), but it has not
> yet been validated against a live Chrome by the maintainers.
> [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md) is the trial guide — please report what
> works and what does not.

### Prerequisites

- DeepSeek Harness (any profile; see Install for the desktop-App caveat)
- Google Chrome **or** Microsoft Edge
- Node.js >= 18 on the machine that runs DSH (the plugin is an ESM package;
  the DSH host provides the runtime — you only need Node present if you use
  the manual bundle install, which runs `pnpm install`)
- **You must restart Chrome once** with the debug port the first time — or
  let the plugin do it (see Auto-launch). Chrome only opens the debug port at
  launch, so an already-running Chrome without the port must be restarted.

### Install

The repo is a standard DSH bundle (`package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`), and the compiled output ships in
`lib/` — clone-and-use, no build step needed.

**Which install command works depends on which DSH surface you use**
(verified against DSH 0.2.1-rc.5):

| You use | Install command |
|---|---|
| CLI / `web` / `headless` / custom profile | `dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:AI-J-IN/dsh-ga-browser-bridge` |
| Desktop App (`desktop` profile) | See "Desktop App users" below |

```bash
# CLI / web / headless / custom profile — one command, bundle patch auto-applied
dsh plugin --profile web add github:AI-J-IN/dsh-ga-browser-bridge

# local directory (after git clone)
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-ga-browser-bridge
```

**Desktop App users.** The `dsh` CLI refuses to manage the reserved
`desktop` profile (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron
application`), and the App's built-in bundle installer accepts npm-registry
URLs only — a GitHub tarball URL is not accepted. Two working options:

1. **Recommended: install into a CLI-managed profile** alongside the
   desktop App (profiles are independent; e.g. `dsh plugin --profile web
   add github:AI-J-IN/dsh-ga-browser-bridge`, then `dsh --profile web`).
2. **Manual bundle install into desktop** (about 3 minutes):
   ```powershell
   git clone https://github.com/AI-J-IN/dsh-ga-browser-bridge.git
   # copy the package dir into the desktop profile's node_modules
   Copy-Item -Recurse -Force dsh-ga-browser-bridge "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-ga-browser-bridge"
   ```
   then append the bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` content (one insert row,
   see Configuration) to
   `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\cordis.patch.yml`, and restart the
   Desktop App. The row id `ga-browser-bridge` must not collide with the
   legacy MCP row — disable that row first (see next section).
   The package needs the `ws` module resolvable from the profile's
   node_modules (already present in shipped profiles; if missing, run
   `pnpm add ws` inside the profile directory).

> Note: `dsh plugin add` forwards to `pnpm` in the profile directory, so
> `github:user/repo` specs are resolved by pnpm. The plugin runtime itself
> runs inside the DSH host process (Node >= 22); a separate Node install is
> only needed for the manual bundle path, which runs `pnpm install`.

### Configuration

The bundle inserts one row into your profile composition:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: ga-browser-bridge
      name: dsh-ga-browser-bridge
      config:
        # host: '127.0.0.1'
        # port: 9222
        # autoLaunchChrome: true
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `host` | `127.0.0.1` | CDP debug host |
| `port` | `9222` | CDP debug port |
| `autoLaunchChrome` | `true` | When the port is closed, launch Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port` (reusing your default profile). `false` = fail fast with the exact command to run yourself. |

### The five tools

All names, parameters and return shapes match the legacy bridge.

**`browser_tabs`** — list / find / switch / create / close tabs

```jsonc
{ "action": "list" }                                  // {"count":N,"tabs":[{id,title,url}]}
{ "action": "find", "url_pattern": "github" }         // {"matched":N,"tabs":[...]}
{ "action": "switch", "tab_id": "12" }
{ "action": "create", "url": "https://x.com", "active": true }
{ "action": "close", "tab_id": "12" }
```

**`browser_scan`** — simplified HTML of the current page (script/style/
noscript/svg removed); `text_only:true` returns visible text;
`maxchars` (default 35000) truncates.

**`browser_execute_js`** — run JS in the page, `awaitPromise` supported,
returns the evaluated value. (The legacy DOM-diff monitor is not provided.)

**`browser_cdp`** — raw CDP: `{method, params}` or `{commands:[...]}` batch
with `$N.path` references to earlier results.

**`browser_cookies`** — cookies for the tab's origin, **including HttpOnly**.

### Chrome 136+ restriction (IMPORTANT)

**Chrome 136 and newer refuse to open a remote-debugging port on the DEFAULT
profile.** Passing `--remote-debugging-port` without a *separate*
`--user-data-dir` is **silently ignored**: no error, no port, no
`DevToolsActivePort` file — externally it looks exactly like a typo, which
makes this very hard to diagnose. (Official notice:
[Chrome for Developers — remote debugging switch change](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/remote-debugging-port))

Practical consequences:

- The plugin's auto-launch **cannot** reuse your everyday profile on Chrome
  136+. It detects the installed major version and fails fast with an explicit
  message instead of spawning a Chrome that can never open the port.
- Point the plugin at a **separate profile directory** via
  `DSH_BROWSER_USER_DATA_DIR`, or start Chrome yourself with
  `--user-data-dir=<separate dir>`.
- A separate profile starts with no logins. To carry sessions over, copy these
  from your real profile (Chrome closed): `Network\Cookies`, `Login Data`,
  `Login Data For Account`, `Web Data`, `Preferences`, `Secure Preferences`,
  `Bookmarks`, plus `User Data\Local State` — that last file holds the DPAPI
  key that decrypts the cookie database; without it the copied cookies are
  unreadable.

```bat
REM Windows: a dedicated debug profile
"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" ^
  --remote-debugging-port=9222 ^
  --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 ^
  --user-data-dir="%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data DSH" ^
  --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check
```

Then point the plugin at the same directory so auto-launch agrees:

```powershell
setx DSH_BROWSER_USER_DATA_DIR "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data DSH"
```

### Auto-launch & login state

When the plugin finds the debug port closed it launches Chrome itself with
`--remote-debugging-port`. On Chrome **< 136** it reuses your real profile
(no `--user-data-dir`) so every login is preserved; on **136+** that is
impossible (see the section above), so it requires a separate profile.

1. If your Chrome is **already running without the debug port**, Chrome will
   not open the port on the existing process. The plugin then reports the
   exact fix: close all Chrome windows and let it relaunch (or set
   `DSH_BROWSER_USER_DATA_DIR` to a separate profile). It will **never kill
   your browser**.
2. The first relaunch restores your tabs (Chrome's own restore).

To launch manually instead (Windows) — include `--user-data-dir` on Chrome 136+,
otherwise the port silently never opens:

```bat
"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" --remote-debugging-port=9222 --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 --user-data-dir="%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data DSH"
```

macOS / Linux:

```bash
google-chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222 --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 \
  --user-data-dir="$HOME/.config/google-chrome-dsh"
```

Environment overrides (take precedence over config): `DSH_BROWSER_PATH`
(or `CHROME_PATH`), `DSH_BROWSER_USER_DATA_DIR`, `DSH_BROWSER_PORT`.

### Do not mount both bridges

The legacy `ga-browser-bridge` MCP row and this plugin register the **same
`browser_*` tool names**. Disable or remove the legacy row
(`serverName: ga-browser-bridge` / `br_mcp.py`) from your
`cordis.patch.yml` before installing this plugin.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / Fix |
|---|---|
| `No browser tabs available` | Chrome not running with the debug port. Let auto-launch work, or run the manual command above. |
| `Chrome is already running without a debug port` | Close all Chrome windows, then retry. The plugin will not kill it for you. |
| Tool appears but every call times out | Another process owns port 9222; check `netstat -ano \| findstr 9222`, or set a different `port`. |
| Login state missing | The plugin launched Chrome with a separate profile. Set `DSH_BROWSER_USER_DATA_DIR` to your real profile dir, or don't override it at all. |
| `browser_execute_js` returns `[error] ...` | The page threw; the message contains the JS exception. Split navigation and action into two calls. |
| `error: profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application` | DSH platform limitation, not a plugin bug: the `dsh` CLI cannot manage the desktop App's reserved profile. Install into a CLI-managed profile, or use the manual bundle steps in Install. |
| `install_bundle` times out with `/-/npm/v1/attestations/... ETIMEDOUT` | The App's bundle installer expects an npm registry URL; it does not accept GitHub tarball URLs. Use the CLI (`dsh plugin ... add github:...`) or the manual bundle steps. |
| Plugin installed but tools missing after restart | Tool rows register at startup only — fully restart the DSH App/session after installing. Also confirm the legacy `ga-browser-bridge` MCP row is disabled (same tool names). |
| DSH fails to activate: `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'host')` | Fixed in 0.1.1: the loader passes `null` config for an entry with no `config:` key. Update the plugin (or add an explicit `config: {}`). |
| `--remote-debugging-port` given but the port never opens, no error | Chrome 136+ restriction: a separate `--user-data-dir` is mandatory. See "Chrome 136+ restriction". |
| `'Network.getAllCookies' wasn't found` | Fixed in 0.1.1: Chrome 155 removed it; the plugin now uses `Storage.getCookies` (falls back on old Chrome). |
| `newTab` hangs / `GET /json/new` 405 | Fixed in 0.1.1: `/json/new` requires PUT. |
| `activate`/`close` fail with `Unexpected token 'T', "Target activated"` | Fixed in 0.1.1: those endpoints return plain text, not JSON. |

### Development

Contributor workflow (end users do not need this — `lib/` is committed):

```bash
npm install
npm run build     # tsc -> lib/ (only after changing src/)
npm test          # jest (mocked CDP; no real Chrome needed)
```

### License

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# computer-use-codex2dsh

> Give [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (DSH) full Windows desktop control: 13 `sky__*` tools backed by an **open-source native reimplementation** of the Sky computer-use helper — no ChatGPT/Codex installation required at runtime.

`computer-use-codex2dsh` 是一个独立的 Windows「电脑操作」Cordis 插件：它把开源原生引擎 `sky-engine`（`engine/`，Rust，逆向复刻 Sky `codex-computer-use.exe` 的 stdio JSON-RPC 契约）接到 DeepSeek Harness 上，让模型可以直接查看窗口、点击、打字、滚动、拖拽。插件自身是一个纯 Node.js 的 stdio JSON-RPC 客户端/监管者——**运行时不连接 ChatGPT/Codex 的任何服务，不读取任何账号数据，不使用网络**。

## 它做什么

- 向 Harness 注册 13 个 `sky__*` 桌面工具（见下表），独占 `computerUse` 注册槽位。
- 首次调用时把 `sky-engine` 与一个本地 `app-server` 桩进程暂存到 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-computer-use\bin`，以 `--parent-pid` 方式启动并监管；卸载插件时干净回收进程。
- 结果经 MCP 适配器投影：截图作为图像附件、UIA 树带元素索引；插件层补充了新鲜快照校验、遮挡启发式拒绝、自我排除等守卫。

## 引擎：`engine/`（sky-rs）

`engine/` 是 `codex-computer-use.exe` 的行为兼容开源重实现（Rust，`windows` + `uiautomation` crate）：

- 完整的 20 方法 RPC 面（`list_apps` / `list_windows` / `get_window` / `get_window_state` / `activate_window` / `click` / `click_element` / `scroll_element` / `drag` / `scroll` / `type_text` / `press_key` / `set_value` / `perform_secondary_action` / `launch_app` / `end_turn` / `close` / `diagnostic_state` / `start|stop_audio_recording`），逐条对齐 `SKY_WINDOWS_PROTOCOL_SPEC.md` 的错误文案、审批/回合/预算 meta、130/Esc 中断标记等语义；
- 窗口/应用枚举（含 taskbar AUMID 探测、StartApps/UserAssist 使用度）、WGC 窗口截图（WIC JPEG 编码）、UIA 元素树与 pattern 动作、SendInput 输入、app-server 握手与策略查询、受限环境变量强化、快照缓存与 `diagnostic_state`。

构建（Windows，[Rust toolchain](https://rustup.rs/)）：

```sh
cd engine && cargo build --release
# 产物：engine/target/release/sky-engine.exe
```

然后把它接到插件（配置任选其一）：

```yaml
# cordis.patch.yml 的 pluginConfig
helperPath: "C:/path/to/engine/target/release/sky-engine.exe"
```

不设 `helperPath` 时插件仍会自动发现本机已安装的 Codex/ChatGPT 桌面版自带的原版助手——两条路线都支持。

## 工具一览

| 工具 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| `sky__list_apps` / `sky__list_windows` / `sky__get_window` | 枚举应用与窗口，解析窗口句柄 `{app, id}` |
| `sky__get_window_state` | 一次调用同时取 JPEG 截图与 UIA 可访问性树（元素索引仅对该快照有效） |
| `sky__activate_window` | 置前窗口（任何输入前的必要动作——输入发往前台窗口） |
| `sky__click` | 元素索引点击（首选）或快照坐标点击（必须携带 `screenshotId`） |
| `sky__drag` / `sky__scroll` | 快照坐标拖拽 / 滚动（必须携带 `screenshotId`） |
| `sky__type_text` / `sky__press_key` | 字面文本输入 / 组合键（`Enter`、`ctrl+s` 等） |
| `sky__set_value` / `sky__perform_secondary_action` | UIA 值模式写入 / 次级动作（Raise、Scroll Up/Down/Left/Right、Expand、Collapse） |
| `sky__launch_app` | 按应用 id、AUMID、可执行文件路径或应用名启动应用 |

## 前置要求

- **Windows 10/11**（桌面自动化仅存在于 Windows）。
- **DeepSeek Harness**（提供 `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `~4.0.5`、`dsh-tools` / `dsh-system-prompt` / `dsh-computer-use` `0.2.1-rc.5` 等 peer 依赖的宿主环境）。
- **Node.js**（`node.exe`，用于运行本地 `app-server` 桩；可用 `nodePath` 指定）。
- 使用内置开源引擎时**无需**安装 OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT 桌面版。

## 安装

把本仓库放进 DSH profile 可解析的位置后，用 Harness 的 plugin manager 安装，或直接把 `cordis.patch.yml` 的两条 `insert` 合并进你的 profile composition，并让 `name:` 指向本包（`computer-use-codex2dsh`）。插件平台标记为 `win32`。

## 配置

| 选项 | 默认 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| `helperPath` | 自动发现 | 助手二进制绝对路径——推荐指向 `engine/target/release/sky-engine.exe`；留空则自动发现本机 Codex/ChatGPT 桌面版原版助手 |
| `nodePath` | 自动发现 | 用于运行 app-server 桩的 `node.exe` |
| `stageDir` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-computer-use\bin` | 助手/桩的暂存目录（须为 Medium 完整性级别） |
| `codexHome` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-computer-use\codex-home` | 助手的私有 CODEX_HOME（中断标记、缓存） |
| `autoApprove` | `[]` | 免审批应用。大小写不敏感，接受助手报告的任意身份：app id、`process:<path>`、可执行文件名（`notepad` / `notepad.exe`）、AUMID 包前缀（`Microsoft.WindowsNotepad`）、含本地化的显示名（`记事本`）。Harness 自身永远不会被批准 |
| `enforceBrowserUrlPolicy` | `false` | 为 `true` 时不再发送绕过助手浏览器 URL 策略的本地测试 meta |
| `timeoutMs` / `launchTimeoutMs` | `10000` / `15000` | 单请求 / 启动超时 |

## 安全模型

- **逐应用审批（fail-closed）**：助手首次触达某个应用时发出 `approvalRequest`，经 Harness 审批服务征询用户；没有审批服务或用户拒绝时一律拒绝。`allowed-once` 在同一 agent 会话内记住。
- **不可覆盖的自我排除**：任何输入类工具（点击/输入/按键/激活等）与审批层三重拒绝把 Harness 自己当作目标，`autoApprove` 也无法解锁。
- **物理 Esc**：助手以 130 退出并写入中断标记后，本回合内所有调用短路为「用户已停止电脑操作」；回合推进或标记被清理即自动恢复。
- **坐标守卫**：坐标输入必须携带该窗口最新快照的 `screenshotId`；快照期被窗口级覆盖物压住的点直接拒绝（目标应用自己的小菜单不误伤）。任何输入送达后旧快照坐标即失效。
- 桌面操作对模型可见的护栏只是护栏：请在人工可监督的前提下使用。

## 已知限制（实测）

- 部分现代应用不向助手暴露完整 UIA 树（视窗口状态而定）→ 用截图 + 坐标/键盘驱动。
- 进程被系统挂起时（锁屏会话），UIA provider 连接可能只回顶层节点；引擎已按原版行为做 structure-changed 事件订阅唤醒（`wake_provider`），极端场景下树覆盖仍可能少于原版——解锁后进程恢复即正常。
- 已知线级偏差：`approvalRequest` 的 JSON 字段顺序与原版不同（字母序 vs 结构定义序），JSON 语义等价，对所有解析方透明。
- `explorer.exe` 等共享系统进程的窗口报 `executable has multiple signatures`，无法寻址。
- 锁屏会话期间截图返回权限错误并降级为无截图（与原版行为一致）。
- 遮挡检测是尽力而为：只有当快照同时捕获到覆盖窗口时才能判定；输入前务必先 `sky__activate_window`。

## 协议逆向依据

`SKY_WINDOWS_PROTOCOL_SPEC.md` 记录了对原版 `codex-computer-use.exe`（Rust 原生二进制）的全部逆向证据：20 方法名单、审批流、中断标记、浏览器 URL 策略门禁、枚举身份、截图/输入语义及全部锚点地址。`engine/` 以该 spec 为行为基准，并通过与原版助手的 A/B 差分探针验证一致性。

## 免责声明

非官方爱好者项目，与 OpenAI、DeepSeek 无关。`engine/` 为本仓库原创代码；原版 `codex-computer-use.exe`（如你选择使用）及其行为归上游所有，请遵守上游许可与服务条款。

# ds-bot

The DS Bot plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh). It turns dsh into a team of long-lived Bots that talk to you, to each other and in group chats. See the [project page](../README.md) for an overview, install steps and screenshots.

> Early release (v0.1). Features, tools and the saved data format can still change.

Tested with dsh `0.2.1-rc.4` (Web) and `0.2.0-rc.2` (Web and Desktop).

## Features

- **Long-lived Bots**: each Bot is a dsh Session in the "DS Bot" workspace, with its own name, role, instructions and model.
- **Working folders**: a Bot can work in a folder you choose instead of the team workspace, and a group chat can set one folder for all its members there. Pick it in the Bot's settings or details panel or in the group's settings, or ask a Bot (`update_bot`, `update_group`). After a change, the chat goes on in a fresh part that starts in the new folder. When a Bot sets a folder outside the team workspace, or adds a Bot to a group that works in one, it asks for your approval if those Bots can only write in their folder. Folders that hold dsh data (`$DSH_HOME`, the team's data) are refused. The team workspace itself moves in Settings > General > Locations; Bots and groups that work there go on in a fresh part in the new folder, and the old folder keeps its files.
- **Permission presets**: each Bot runs with its own dsh permission preset (Read only, Workspace or Full access), set in its details panel. A group chat can run all its members with one preset there, in place of their own: turn on **Same for every member** under Permissions in the group's settings. Only you set permissions; Bots cannot change them.
- **Bots work together**: `message_bot` sends a message to another Bot, `create_bot` and `update_bot` add and set up Bots (including a profile photo from a local image file or a data URL), and `ask_user` asks you a question without blocking the other Bots. `show_view` draws a card in a Bot's own chat — text, metrics, tables, progress, choices, confirmations and short forms; an interactive card waits for your answer.
- **Group chats**: members speak one at a time, and each one reads the latest messages first. A message can `@Name` a member to pass the turn on; type `@` to pick one from a list. **+ → Reference a chat** adds another Bot's chat to a message as context, and in a group the members who answer get it. A member with nothing new to add stays quiet (`[PASS]`). Each member has its own hidden Session per group, so a group never reads a Bot's private chat.
- **Roles and permissions**:

  | Who | Can do |
  |---|---|
  | You | Everything |
  | Main Bot (there can be more than one) | Manage every group; change and delete Bots |
  | Group admin | Manage its own group only (name, notice, members, reply mode) |
  | Member | Speak in the group, `@` another member, and post into its groups from outside them |

- **Long chats stay inside the model's window**: dsh's own compaction never runs on a Bot's Session. When a turn ends past the check line (a share of the model's context window), a small separate model call, the context steward, reads the latest messages of the chat and decides once. If the work is still under way, the chat is condensed in place into a checkpoint: a handoff summary plus your recent messages word for word. If the work has reached a stopping point, the Bot writes a handoff note and continues in a new part. Either way you still see one chat, with no marker. Earlier parts and condensed messages stay searchable in a full-text index (`node:sqlite` FTS5) through `read_own_chat`.
- **Memory**: each Bot keeps notes across all its conversations, each group chat keeps its own for its members, and the team shares one more. See [Memory](#memory).
- **Web search**: see [Web search](#web-search).
- **Bot browser (dsh Desktop and the desktop app)**: see [Bot browser](#bot-browser).
- **Images**: for a model that cannot read images, a vision model first turns the image into text.
- **Secrets**: a Bot asks for an API key or token with a card in its own chat and never sees the value. See [Secrets](#secrets).
- **Usage**: Settings → Usage shows token usage by time (24 hours to 12 months, or days picked on a calendar), by Bot and by model, with a page for each Bot and each model. Calls that a Session logs are read from the logs, so older chats count too. Calls that leave no log (checkpoints, handoff notes, the steward, image readings, dsh titles and compaction) are counted while they stream, from the time the plugin runs. Tokens only, no cost.
- **Make it yours**: name, role, instructions, model and look (20 characters and 12 colors, or your own photo) for each Bot; a theme, an accent color and an avatar animation level (quiet, normal or lively) for the team. A pinned Bot or group chat shows a small pushpin in the sidebar. Settings has these pages: General (look), Bots (Main Bots and each Bot's settings), Group chats (each group's settings), Connectors, Capabilities, Scheduled tasks, Usage, Secrets, Feedback and About DS Bot (versions, updates and links).

## Install

The [project page](../README.md#install) has the full steps for dsh Desktop and dsh Web. In short:

- dsh Desktop: Settings → Plugins → add `ds-bot` (npm), a `.tgz` file, or `github:Fei2411/DS-Bot#v0.1.7&path:/ds-bot`.
- Command line: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add ds-bot` (or `--profile web`).

To work on the plugin from a checkout, add it to a dsh profile as a linked dependency and a bundle:

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "ds-bot": "link:/path/to/ds-bot" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "ds-bot"] } }
}
```

Run `pnpm install` in the profile folder, then start dsh from the deepseek-harness repository:

```sh
pnpm -s dsh --profile web --no-open
```

The first time the team opens, the plugin creates a Main Bot called Chief.

**Upgrading from the legacy `dsh-bot` package**: earlier builds used the package name `dsh-bot`. Remove `dsh-bot` from the profile before you add `ds-bot`, because both use the plugin id `bot`. Your team, chats and secrets stay where they are (see [Data and backups](#data-and-backups)); saved browser settings, the theme and Bot colors move over the first time DS Bot opens.

## Configuration

Options go in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, under the `bot` entry. All of them are optional.

```yaml
- id: bot
  name: ds-bot
  config:
    workspace: /path/to/workspace   # where the Bots work; default <home>/workspace
    home: /path/to/bot-data         # where the team is saved; default $DSH_HOME/bot
    checkRatio: 0.8                 # share of the model's usable window where the steward decides
    browser: true                   # force the Bot browser on or off; default on in Desktop and the desktop app only
    memory: true                    # false turns memory off: no memory tools, section or panel
    memoryReview: true              # false leaves memory to the Bots' own remember calls
    diagnosticsFile: false          # keep the error log in memory only; default <home>/logs/diagnostics.jsonl
    updateCheck: true               # look for a newer DS Bot when a window opens; default true
    updateRegistry: https://registry.example/   # ask only this npm registry for updates
    github: false                   # hide the GitHub connector; default shown in Connectors
```

**Updates**: when a window opens, DS Bot asks where it was installed from for a newer release: the npm registry (the one the DSH plugin manager installs from, then its fallbacks), or the latest GitHub release for a `github:…#vX.Y.Z` install. A newer version shows a cloud button at the top right of the sidebar; **Update** reinstalls DS Bot through the DSH plugin manager, and the new version runs from the next DSH start. A linked or local checkout is never offered an update. Settings → About DS Bot shows the same state, with **Check for updates** to ask again at once.

The same card can carry DSH itself: a DS Bot release may name the DSH release it was verified against (`dsBot.verifiedDsh` in its `package.json`), and only that version is offered — running something newer is a downgrade offer too. A release that names no version offers no DSH update. A DSH installed from npm is swapped by `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>`. DSH Desktop installs the newest release its own updater finds, so the card shows DSH there only when that release is the verified one, and **Open updates** opens the app's update panel. A release may raise the floor with `dsBot.minBot`: until the bot itself is that new, the DSH row waits.

## Models

Model providers are set up with dsh's `llm-pi-ai` plugin in `cordis.patch.yml`. Every Bot runs on one model of its own, from the models DSH serves. A new team's first Main Bot has none: its chat opens on a model card and it greets the user only after a pick. The Create Bot form starts on the DSH default model. The Bot's details panel and settings (or a Main Bot's `update_bot`) change it; a Bot whose model is no longer served shows the card again. A team saved by an older version keeps the model each Bot last ran on.

- Give every model a `contextWindow`. DS Bot takes its lines from it: the usable window is the window minus the reply reserve (`maxTokens`), the hard line is 95% of that, and the check line is `checkRatio` of it. A model without `contextWindow` gets the adapter's default (262,144 tokens for `llm-pi-ai`), which may be wrong for that model; a model that reports no window at all counts as 500,000.
- To send images, the provider needs `defaultInput: [ text, image ]`.
- Keep API keys out of the repository. Use dsh's own key storage or environment variables.

## Memory

A Bot remembers what should last beyond one conversation: your preferences, decisions, corrections and facts it should not ask again. Memory is plain Markdown in the [Agent Memory Repo](https://github.com/AgentMemoryRepo/agentmemoryrepo) format: one entry per line, ending in `[source: …; added: …]`.

After each turn, a memory review reads what is new in the conversation and keeps, updates or removes entries itself, so memory does not depend on the Bot deciding to call `remember`. A Bot's own chat is reviewed by its model into its own memory; a group chat is reviewed once for the whole group, by the admin's model (or the first member's), into the group memory only. It keeps only what you say, writes entries in your language, and refuses keys, passwords and ID numbers.

- **Three scopes**: each Bot has its own memory; each group chat has a group memory, which its members read in that group only (not in their own chats, and not in other groups); and the team memory is read by every Bot. A Bot writes its own, and any member writes its group's memory from the group. Main Bots and group admins (of any group) also write the team memory; a Main Bot can read and change another Bot's memory when you ask.
- **Tools**: `remember` saves an entry or replaces one (`replace`), `forget` removes one, and `recall` searches every entry, reads a topic whole, or lists what is saved. In a Bot's own chat they use its own memory by default; in a group chat, the group memory (`scope: "own"` for the Bot's own). The Bot adds the source (a part anchor such as `part 2 #1234`, which `read_own_chat` opens, or the group and the time) and the date; a Bot that writes for others is named with `by:`.
- **Files**: `MEMORY.md` holds what every conversation needs, and details go in topic files linked from its `## Index` as `[[topic]]`.
- **In the prompt**: the Bot's own and the team's `MEMORY.md` go into the Bot's system prompt, and in a group Session the group's after them. The section is frozen when a Session starts, so the provider's prompt cache holds; a change shows from the next part or checkpoint, and `recall` finds it at once.
- **Fixed sizes**: an entry has at most 300 characters, a `MEMORY.md` 4,000, a topic 16,000, and a scope 40 topics. A save past a limit fails and says how to make room.
- **Safety**: memory is data, not instructions. An entry that looks like a key or token is refused, and a Bot is told not to save what a web page, file or tool result asks it to remember.
- **History**: files change in place, and `journal.jsonl` keeps every change with the line before and after. When a Bot or a group chat is deleted, its memory moves to `archive/`.

**The memory panel**: the details panel of a Bot, and of a group chat, has a Memory row with the entry count; Manage opens the memory panel. A Bot's panel shows its own memory and the team memory; a group's shows the group memory.

- **Memory summary**: a model writes a short summary in prose from every entry, in the interface language: the Bot's, or for a group its admin's. It is written again when the entries change, and the ⋯ menu can regenerate it.
- **All entries**: the ⋯ menu lists every entry by scope and topic, with its date and author, and the size of each `MEMORY.md`. Remove takes two clicks.
- **Ask or update**: ask what the Bot remembers, or tell it what to add, correct or remove. One model call answers from the entries only, and its changes go through the same checks as the tools.
- A line in the chat ("Memory updated") shows when a Bot changes memory and opens the panel. When memory changes in the background, the capsule at the top of the chat (the Bot's, or the group's) stretches to say "Memory updated" for a moment; clicking it opens the memory panel.

A read-only dsh (see [Data and backups](#data-and-backups)) shows memory but cannot change it.

## Web search

The package includes a second plugin, `ds-bot/web-search`. It registers the search provider `auto`, and `cordis.patch.yml` makes it the default. Each search goes in this order:

1. If the profile names another `searchProvider`, that one is used.
2. The current model route's own search, with that route's key and host. The plugin knows the Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses and Gemini protocols, and a few search APIs (Ollama, Kimi, Zhipu, MiMo). Add more with `searchApis`.
3. A fallback without a key: the public result pages of Bing and DuckDuckGo.
4. If nothing works, the search fails and tells the model not to guess addresses.

Each result starts with a `Search backend: …` line that names the path it took.

**Turning `auto` off**: the `web` row still names `auto` when you turn off only the `web-search-auto` row (in the sidebar's Plugins page or with `disabled: true` in a profile patch). Then `web_search` fails in every session, Bot or not, with `WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_MISSING` (`configured web provider "auto" is not registered`). When you turn that row off, also name another `searchProvider` for the `web` row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. The override replaces the row's whole config, so restate `fetchProvider`:

```yaml
- id: web-search-auto
  name: ds-bot/web-search
  disabled: true
- id: web
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-web'
  config:
    searchProvider: deepseek-official
    fetchProvider: http
```

Another plugin can also set the search provider while dsh runs, after the profile patch. When you turn such a plugin off, check this setting again.

## Bot browser

In dsh Desktop and the desktop app, a Bot's chat header has a globe button. It opens that Bot's own browser panel.

- **One partition per Bot** (`bot:<id>`): logins and cookies belong to that Bot only. The desktop app keeps them on disk, so a Bot stays signed in after a restart; dsh Desktop keeps them in memory only.
- **The Bot can read the page**: the `read_browser` tool reads the page's DOM, not a screenshot. The text becomes Markdown with headings, nested lists, tables, code blocks and quotes. Links and form controls are marked `[#n]` in place and listed below with their targets and values. The tool also reads the text you selected. Long pages are read in parts (`from`). Page content is treated as data, never as instructions.
  - It reads open Shadow DOM (with `<slot>`) and same-origin iframes up to 3 levels deep.
  - It reads only what is visible: `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, zero-height and closed `<details>` content is skipped.
  - It never reads the values of password, credit card (`autocomplete="cc-*"`) or one-time code fields.
  - Limits: 400,000 characters, 150,000 nodes, 5,000 rows per table, 3,000 links and controls, 1.5 seconds. A cut result says so.
  - It cannot read cross-origin iframes (one line with the address), closed shadow roots, canvas content (online editors, maps), or text in CSS `::before` / `::after`. On pages that render on demand, only the rendered part is read.
  - Read only: the Bot cannot click, type, scroll or open addresses yet.
- **Addresses**: http and https only. localhost and LAN addresses are allowed; cloud metadata addresses (such as `169.254.x.x`) and dsh's own ports are not.
- The browser panel and the details drawer share the right column; opening one closes the other. Switching chats switches the panel to that Bot. Deleting a Bot clears its browser and saved address.
- **Cookie import (desktop app only)**: the import button in the browser bar previews the cookies of a file (Cookie-Editor JSON, Netscape `cookies.txt`, Playwright `storageState`) or of an installed Chromium/Firefox profile, then writes them into the Bot's partition. A source browser closes for a moment so its cookie store can be copied, and it reopens with its tabs. Sign-in that lives outside cookies (localStorage, passkeys) does not come along.

dsh Web has no browser panel and no `read_browser` tool.

## Secrets

When a Bot needs an API key, token or password, it calls `request_secret`, and a secret card shows in its own chat. The Bot never sees the value.

- **Fill in**: the field hides what you type, is not part of a form and is not autofilled. Choose "All Bots" or "Only this Bot" and select Save. A value must have at least 4 characters (a 4-digit PIN works). A value of 8 characters or more is hidden wherever it appears; a shorter one only where no letter or digit touches it, so ordinary words stay intact.
- **Allow**: if the secret is already saved but this Bot is not allowed to use it, the card only asks whether to allow it. You can also replace the value there.
- **Use**: the value goes into the Bot's shell environment as `DSH_SECRET_<NAME>` (`$DSH_SECRET_NAME` in bash, `$env:DSH_SECRET_NAME` in PowerShell). `list_secrets` lists the names a Bot can use. An MCP capability can also take `$DSH_SECRET_<NAME>` in its env, its headers and its URL (path or query); in the URL the value is URL-encoded. Use headers when the server accepts them.
- **Masking**: before a tool result is saved and before each request goes to the model, every copy of a secret value is replaced with `[secret:<NAME>]`.
- **Manage**: Settings → Secrets lists every secret by name, purpose, the Bot that asked and the last use. You can change who may use it, replace the value, delete it or add one. Deleting a Bot removes it from every secret.
- **Storage**: `<DSH_HOME>/bot/secrets.json`, file mode 600, written atomically. Values are never in `state.json` or logs.

Limits:

- On Windows, the file mode has no effect; the file is protected by your user folder only.
- Only exact copies of a value are masked. A Bot that encodes, splits or reverses a value can still print it. Do not give important secrets to a Bot you do not trust.
- On a page that is not HTTPS (for example dsh Web opened over http on a LAN), the value crosses the network in clear text. The card warns you.
- Group chats show no cards; a Bot asks in its own chat.

## Data and backups

The plugin saves its data in `config.home`. Without it, the folder is `$DSH_HOME/bot`, or `~/.dsh/bot` when `DSH_HOME` is not set.

| System | Default folder |
|---|---|
| Linux, macOS | `~/.dsh/bot/` |
| Windows | `C:\Users\<user>\.dsh\bot\` |

- To move all dsh data (Sessions, profiles and plugin data), set `DSH_HOME`.
- To move only the plugin data, set `home` in the configuration (see [Configuration](#configuration)).

Files in `bot/`:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `state.json` | The team: Bots, groups, Bot-to-Bot messages, preferences and open questions. A long message keeps only its first 2,000 characters here; all of it is in the Session it went to. |
| `group-lines/` | Long group lines, up to the 20,000 characters a member reads, one file per line; each is removed when its line leaves the group's latest 60 lines or the group is deleted |
| `handoff-results/` | The whole result of a piece of work a Bot handed on, when it is longer than the 2,000 characters `state.json` keeps, one file per result; each is removed once the answer it went into has gone up |
| `state.lock` | The dsh that is using this data (pid and host), its mtime bumped as a heartbeat. It is removed when that dsh exits; a leftover whose heartbeat has stopped is taken over by the next dsh to load. |
| `chat-index.sqlite` | Full-text index of older chat parts (`read_own_chat`); rebuilt if deleted |
| `usage.sqlite` | Token counts for the Usage page; rebuilt from the Session logs if deleted, losing only the calls outside the logs and the names of deleted Bots |
| `memory/` | Memory (see [Memory](#memory)): `bots/<id>/`, `groups/<id>/` and `team/` (`MEMORY.md` and topics), `journal.jsonl` (every change), `snapshots/` (the section each Session froze), `summaries/` (the panel's summary; safe to delete), `reviewed.json` (how far the memory review has read) and `archive/` (deleted Bots and group chats) |
| `ocr.json` | Cache of image text; safe to delete |
| `avatars/` | The avatar library: the profile photos you imported once, so several Bots can use the same picture. `index.json` lists them, `files/` holds the images, each named by the hash of its bytes, so the same photo is stored once. The Bots that use a photo keep their own copy. Safe to delete. |
| `workspace` | The team workspace: the working folder of every Bot without one of its own (`config.workspace` changes it) |
| `secrets.json` | Saved secrets. Treat backups of it like passwords. |
| `logs/diagnostics.jsonl` | Recent errors and warnings, with keys, tokens, saved secrets and the home folder removed. It moves to `diagnostics.jsonl.1` past 1 MB. Safe to delete. |

The chats themselves are dsh Sessions and are not in `bot/`: they are in `~/.dsh/sessions/`. dsh keeps its workspace list in `~/.dsh/storages/workspace.json` and profiles (with model settings) in `~/.dsh/profiles/`. dsh Desktop keeps each Bot's browser partition in memory only, so its logins are not saved. The desktop app saves them with its own window data, not in the data location, and clears a Bot's when the Bot is deleted.

**Back up and restore**

1. Quit dsh completely (both the Web server and Desktop), so `state.json` is current.
2. Copy all of `~/.dsh/` (at least `bot/`, `sessions/` and `storages/`). A copy of `bot/` alone loses the chats.
3. To restore, quit dsh, put the folder back in the same place, then start dsh.

**Move to another computer**: `state.json` has no absolute paths except the working folders you set for Bots and groups, but dsh's `storages/workspace.json` and the Session folder names contain the workspace's absolute path. If the path is the same on the new computer, copy the folder. If it is different (another user name or system), it is not yet tested whether dsh finds the old Sessions.

**dsh Web and Desktop at the same time**: by default both use the same `~/.dsh`. The dsh that loads the team first takes `bot/state.lock` and can change the team. The other one is read-only: it shows the team and follows changes to the file, but refuses changes (`bot/read-only`, "open in another dsh"), and its Bots cannot start new Sessions. When the first one exits, the other one takes over on its next request. To change the team from both at once, give one of them a different `DSH_HOME` (two separate teams).

## Development

You need Node 24, pnpm and a deepseek-harness checkout with its dependencies installed, next to this repository (`../deepseek-harness`, or set `DSH_HARNESS`). The Desktop test bench also needs `xvfb-run` and `ffmpeg`. Web screenshots need Chrome or Chromium (`CHROME_BIN`; by default `google-chrome` or `chromium`).

```sh
npm ci                                   # esbuild, for the client build
npm run build                            # src/client → client.js
npm test                                 # unit tests
npm run lint                             # oxlint from the dsh repository (.oxlintrc.json)
dev/bench.sh dev 3100 8800 start         # Web test bench: mock model + dsh Web, data in ../.dsh-test-dev
dev/desktop-linux/desktop.sh dev start   # Desktop test bench: mock model + dsh Desktop in Xvfb
CONTEXT_WINDOW=100000 CHECK_RATIO=0.45 dev/bench.sh smoke 3101 8801 reset && node dev/smoke.mjs smoke 3101
dev/check.sh                             # all checks (see below)
```

- `client.js` is built from `src/client/` and committed, so `link:` and Git installs need no build. Do not edit `client.js` by hand; `npm test` checks that it matches the source. After a change in `src/client/`, run `npm run build` and reload the page. After a change in `index.js` or `src/host/`, restart dsh.
- **Web test bench** `dev/bench.sh <name> <web port> <mock port> [start|stop|reset|status]`: a scripted mock model (`dev/mock-llm.mjs`, no real tokens; its commands are listed at the top of the file) and a dsh Web server. Data goes in `../.dsh-test-<name>/`; `reset` clears the team and Sessions first. The login address with its token is in `../.dsh-test-<name>/web.log`.
- **Desktop test bench** `dev/desktop-linux/desktop.sh <name> [start|stop|reset|status]`: dsh does not run Desktop on Linux; `launch.mts` runs the unpackaged Desktop in Xvfb. The first start downloads Electron and a Linux runtime (a few minutes). `start` returns when the team shows in a 1400×860 window.
- **All checks** `dev/check.sh [--skip steps] [--only steps] [--out dir]`: `unit`, `build`, `lint`, `smoke`, `web` (screenshots of the sidebar, a chat, a group, Bot settings, the Bots page and group settings) and `desktop` (the same screenshots, then the Bot browser checks). It stops everything it started. On failure it names the step and its log and exits non-zero. A full run takes about 3 minutes after the first download.
- **Ports**: every script takes `SLOT=n` (0-9, default 0) so that several people or sessions on one machine do not collide: Web bench `31n0` and mock `88n0`, smoke `31n1` and `88n1`, Desktop mock `88n2`, and so on. A Desktop uses about 1 GB of memory; stop it when you are done.
- **Real models** (these cost tokens): `dev/steward-eval.mjs` sends hand-written conversation endings through the context steward's own prompt to an OpenAI-compatible route (or, with `--api messages`, an Anthropic Messages route such as DeepSeek's official one) and checks each decision. `dev/llm-tap.mjs <port> <upstream base URL> <log.jsonl> [body dir]` is a logging pass-through for either format: point a provider's `baseURL` at it, and it writes one JSON line per call (steward, checkpoint, handoff note or main turn, the Bot's name, token usage, the answer, and where the request first differs from the same Bot's previous one, which is what a provider's cache can reuse; never headers). With a body dir it also saves every request body. Each file explains its use at the top.
- **Screenshots**: `dev/ui-shots.mjs` works for both apps (`desktop <dsh repo> <dir> <renderer port>` or `web <dsh repo> <dir> <bench name> <web port>`).
- `npm test` loads the `@deepseek-ai/*` packages from the deepseek-harness checkout.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host entry: installs the `src/host/` modules in order |
| `src/host/` | Host: team and storage (`roster`, `store`), tools (`tools`), turns and delivery (`turns`, `delivery`), group chats (`groups`), chat parts, the context steward and the index (`parts`, `steward`, `chat-index`), image text (`images`), secrets (`secrets`), Bot browser (`browser`), the `POST api/bot` route (`channel`) |
| `src/client/` | Browser source: sidebar, chat header, transcript cells, panels and dialogs, themes, Bot browser panel |
| `client.js` | Built from `src/client/` by `scripts/build-client.mjs` (esbuild); committed |
| `web-search.js` | The `auto` search provider; independent of the team code |
| `test/` | Unit tests and fixtures |
| `dev/characters.mjs` | Builds the characters (small 3D models traced to outlines) into the `CHARACTERS` table in `src/client/characters.js` |
| `dev/` | Mock model, test benches, smoke test, Desktop scripts, real-model tools (steward evaluation, logging pass-through) |

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # Model Router · DeepSeek Harness Desktop [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh.md) [![npm version](https://flat.badgen.net/npm/v/@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router) [![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/Alice-Marx/dsh-model-router?lang=en)](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/Alice-Marx/dsh-model-router?ref=badge) [![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/Alice-Marx/dsh-model-router?metric=downloads&lang=en)](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/Alice-Marx/dsh-model-router?ref=badge) [![Listed in the DSH plugin directory](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/alice-marx/dsh-model-router) [![Awesome DSH Plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) [![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/card/Alice-Marx/dsh-model-router?lang=en)](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/Alice-Marx/dsh-model-router?ref=badge) Want release notes only? Click **Watch → Custom → Releases** (you do not need Watching all activity). **Stable release: 0.26.0.** The unified DS Bot + Model Router product ships as one plugin. Upgrading from 0.25.5 adds the Bot team runtime, the official-tool and remote-computer controls, and the packaged desktop app. Install or update through Harness Desktop > Plugins, or with the exact version `@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router@0.26.0`. Preview builds stay on the `preview` tag; `latest` now points at this stable release. A cost-aware model-routing workbench for **DeepSeek Harness Desktop**. Plan locally, compare configured routes, inspect execution permissions, and run dependent work packages through model APIs or supported official vendor CLIs. Stable version: **0.25.5** (`@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router`). This update fixes garbled ZCode TUI box drawing, CJK text and broken color sequences in Windows embedded terminals. Each new ZCode PTY enables UTF-8 before Node starts; system settings remain unchanged. The standalone community ZCode CLI retains both npm and GitHub Release installation methods. It retains the **0.2.1-rc.3** SDK and existing Host peer range. API calls use monetary accounting with daily/monthly budget reservations; subscriptions use a separate book of calls and reported tokens. The workbench shows them as two books that are never added together: one is USD, the other is a call count. Confirmed subscription execution is not blocked only because the API budget is exhausted or API prices are missing. A switch to an API must be priced and admitted before that API call; mixed results retain both channel receipts. The workbench keeps API spending/reservations and subscription usage as two books that are never added, with unknown counters kept unknown. The Bot task page leads with what needs a person (receipts to reconcile, approvals, unconfirmed remote effects, failures, blocked tasks) and stays quiet when the team is healthy. Workbench execution shows live elapsed time and per-package progress, supports cancellation with completed results and reported costs retained, and reconnects to the active job when the panel is reopened. Choose algorithm recommendations or manually assign each decomposed package to an exact model API or official tool, preserving dependencies, refreshed cost previews and retry targets. Routing now supports task-specific quality evidence, joint model/effort selection, historical P90 resource estimates and dependency-aware search. Manual mixed execution is read-only; tools use their configured default model, while the existing editable official-team workflow remains available. Compatibility covers **DeepSeek Harness Desktop 0.2.0-rc.1 / 0.2.0-rc.2 / 0.2.1-rc.2 / 0.2.1-rc.3**, including Hermes/Pi installation and terminal support; neither has a verified managed runner yet. Real vendor execution evidence remains tied to **0.20.0**, with no new model experiments in this release. The router and [GAL](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/deepseek-harness-galgame) have been independent plugins since 0.12.0. Official CLI teamwork runs packages sequentially with dependency context and no automatic model-directory API fallback. Editable teams explicitly choose the Harness sandbox or the vendor CLI's normal environment. In the latter, Git worktrees collect edits but do not restrict OS access. CLIs retain their configured model unless explicitly mapped. See [real Windows validation and its limits](docs/releases/0.20.0-validation.md). Both README versions describe the same interfaces, formulas, defaults and limits. [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) preserves release history. More walkthroughs: [workbench](docs/WORKBENCH_USER_GUIDE.zh.md), [installation](docs/INSTALLATION_GUIDE.zh.md), [migration](docs/archive/MIGRATION.md), and [experiment protocol](docs/ROUTING_SELFTEST_STEPS.zh.md). ## Quick evaluation **One-line value:** A cost-aware DSH workbench for planning tasks, routing model calls, and running dependent work packages with explicit execution permissions. **Category:** **Models & Reasoning** (模型与推理), the best fit in the [community directory's category list](https://www.alldsh.com/categories/); this is a community taxonomy, not an official DSH classification. **Install (DSH Plugin Hub / web profile):** With the DSH CLI available, install the versioned npm package with: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router@0.25.5 ``` **Install in Harness Desktop:** Launch Desktop once to initialize its `desktop` profile, quit Desktop fully, then run: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add @ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router@0.25.5 ``` You can also paste the package spec into **Harness Desktop → Plugins → Add plugin**. Restart Desktop after installation. A global `npm install -g` by itself does not register a Desktop plugin. **Package and entry point:** [`@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router@0.25.5` on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router). The root [`package.json`](package.json) declares the package and bundle patch; [`.dsh-plugin/index.mjs`](.dsh-plugin/index.mjs) exports the required `apply(ctx)` entry point. License: [MIT](LICENSE). **Configuration:** There is no supported import of a user-authored JSON/YAML configuration file. Configure providers, models, and credentials on Harness's **Models** page; configure routing profiles and preferences in the plugin settings. Persistent router state is stored in `$DSH_HOME/model-router/state.json` (default: `~/.dsh/model-router/state.json`). Provider CLIs retain their own login and configuration. The router does not copy API keys into model profiles or terminal logs. **Screenshots and evidence:** The [workbench screenshot](docs/assets/workbench-task-preview.jpg) uses fixture models, prices, and health data; it is a simulated UI preview, not a live Harness or model run. See the [routing workflow diagram](docs/assets/routing-workflow.svg) for the execution flow. The [real Windows validation report](docs/releases/0.20.0-validation.md) documents specific 0.20.0 executions and their limits; 0.25.5 has no verified end-to-end vendor run. The [live progress screenshot](docs/assets/workbench-run-progress.png) is an offline simulation; see the [0.25.0 acceptance report](docs/releases/0.25.0-validation.md) for API/subscription separation and checkpoints, and the [0.25.1 acceptance report](docs/releases/0.25.1-validation.md) for SDK compatibility and validation boundaries. **Permissions and risks:** Planning is local and makes no model call. Execution sends the selected task/context to the chosen model API or vendor CLI and may incur charges. The default Harness-restricted environment separates read-only runs from approved `workspace-write` runs. An explicitly selected `cli-native` editable team runs with the current OS user's permissions, outside the Harness process sandbox; a Git worktree collects changes but does not restrict OS access. External providers and CLI services apply their own data handling and billing terms. **Compatibility:** Declared host support is DeepSeek Harness Desktop **0.2.0-rc.1**, **0.2.0-rc.2**, **0.2.1-rc.2**, and **0.2.1-rc.3**. Source builds pin the published **0.2.1-rc.3** SDK packages; retaining an older peer declaration does not turn offline tests into installed-Desktop acceptance. Node.js **>=22.19** and pnpm **10.34.6** are source development/build requirements, not plugin runtime prerequisites. Compatibility beyond the declared host versions is not claimed. **Contents:** [Quick evaluation](#quick-evaluation) · [Capabilities](#capabilities) · [Install](#install) · [Workbench](#workbench) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Session tools](#session-tools) · [Official tools](#official-tools) · [Team lifecycle](#team-lifecycle) · [Costs](#costs) · [Routing algorithm](#routing) · [Data](#data) · [Development](#development) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) ## What is included | Capability | Current behavior | | --- | --- | | Task planning | Local task classification and complexity analysis; single-route recommendation, dependent team work packages, or an explicit configured model. | | Model configuration | Reads exact `provider/model` routes from Harness; optional user-supplied quality, USD prices, specialties, CLI model names, execution and billing preferences. | | Routing presets | Economy, balanced and quality-first presets; quality floors, estimated token costs and bounded assignment search. Missing prices stay unknown. | | Read-only execution | Preview and confirm a routed run from the workbench, or invoke it in an official Harness session. Supported headless CLIs and model-directory API calls return recorded results. | | Editable CLI execution | A sequential CLI team from the workbench, or one supported CLI from a session, using approved isolated Git worktrees and conditional patch integration. | | Official tools | Detect, install/update, check launch readiness and inspect login status for thirteen registry tools; installation jobs have logs and cancellation. | | Interactive terminal | PowerShell/system shell and all thirteen registry CLI targets (including standalone ZCode CLI TUI), including fixed login commands, live output and multiple sessions. | | Costs and subscriptions | API money and concurrent budget reservations are separate from subscription calls/tokens. Unknown subscription usage stays unknown; API fallback is re-estimated and admitted before the paid call. | | History and quality | Per-package results, dependency views, failure details, rerun/reassignment, ratings and optional stronger-model review. | | Execution boundaries | Shows what each route can read/write and whether its process uses the Harness sandbox. | Generating a route recommendation is local: it does not start a vendor CLI or make a paid model call. Actual execution can incur charges. ![Local planning and official-tool execution](docs/assets/routing-workflow.svg) ## Install in DeepSeek Harness Desktop Open **Plugins → Add plugin** and enter: ```text @ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router@0.25.5 ``` Use the official HTTPS npm source `https://registry.npmjs.org/` when a mirror lacks that exact version. Enable the plugin, then fully quit Harness (including its tray process) and restart it. Plugin details should show **0.25.5** and the sidebar should contain **模型路由** (Model Router). A global `npm install -g` alone does not register a Desktop plugin. You can instead install a local `.tgz` archive or its extracted inner `package` directory through the plugin manager. Both must contain `package.json` and `.dsh-plugin`. See [releases](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/dsh-model-router/releases) for archived builds, or build your own checkout below. ### Upgrade from the old package name The old name `@ljwei-stak/model-router-galgame` ended at 0.13.0. Remove that plugin entry while retaining your profile/application data, then add `@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router@0.25.5`. Do not keep both entries installed: they share the internal plugin id `model-router-galgame` and tool names. The retained id lets existing router settings and history carry over. For the combined 0.11.x package, back up the profile and export the GAL saves you want to preserve before upgrading. Story playback, artwork, music and saves now belong to the independent `@ljwei-stak/dsh-galgame` package. The detailed save limitations are in [MIGRATION.md](docs/archive/MIGRATION.md). ## Use the workbench The workbench groups the workflow into four navigation tabs. Its header summarizes registered routes, detected tools and today's recorded API spending. | Tab | What you do there | | --- | --- | | **任务与执行** — Task and execution | Describe the task, generate advice, choose routed read-only execution or official CLI teamwork, preview and confirm, then inspect history. | | **模型配置** — Model configuration | Refresh/search the model directory and edit exact-route profiles. | | **官方工具** — Official tools | Complete onboarding checks, inspect/install tools and use the interactive terminal. | | **预算与安全** — Budget and security | Manage API money/budgets and separate subscription usage; inspect subscription state and execution boundaries. | Switching tabs keeps the panels mounted, preserving in-progress installation and terminal state. ![0.15.0 workbench preview: task planning and routing advice](docs/assets/workbench-task-preview.jpg) *Screenshot from the local UI preview with fixture models, prices, and health data. No real model or Harness connection was used. Expand a work package to inspect its goal, dependencies, and acceptance checks.* 1. Configure providers, models and credentials on Harness's official **Models** page. In **模型配置**, refresh the directory. A listed route does not prove that its credentials, network or model entitlement work. 2. Optionally enter quality and prices for the routes you want compared. Prices are **USD per million tokens**; quality is a user-supplied **0–100** estimate. Leave unknown prices blank rather than entering zero. 3. In **任务与执行**, describe concrete deliverables, constraints and acceptance criteria. Select **单任务** (single recommendation), **团队分工** (dependent packages for sufficiently complex requests), or **指定模型** (one exact route, without comparing others). Team mode alone does not start any team. 4. Set the per-run estimate target; `0` removes that planning constraint. Click **生成路由建议**. The result appears directly below planning. Check the route, complexity, cost, execution channel and each package's dependencies/checklist. 5. In **在工作台执行**, choose **模型路由（只读）** for the existing routed executor, or first select **团队分工** and choose **官方工具协作**. For official teamwork, select **只读检查** (read-only) or **编辑文件** (edit files). Editable teams also choose **Harness 受限环境** (Harness sandbox, the default) or **厂商 CLI 正常环境** (normal vendor environment, outside the Harness sandbox). Enter an existing absolute workspace path, or reuse the last run's path. Click **预览执行计划**, review each package, its permissions and required confirmations, then explicitly confirm execution. Tick **演练 · 只记录，不执行** (rehearsal) to keep that review and list what each package would call with its estimated cost, while no model, CLI or file is touched; a rehearsal needs no confirmation and records nothing as spent. The Host rechecks the plan before starting; changed conditions can require confirmation again. 6. Inspect **执行记录与子任务** for the actual channel, response, failures, cost and ratings. Official teamwork replans using only installed CLIs ready for the selected permission mode. Edits require approval and a clean Git repository; successful worktree changes are conditionally integrated. An unavailable or failed CLI never silently becomes an API call in this mode. After execution starts, the workbench shows elapsed time, the current package and each package's state. **取消执行** requests cancellation of the active call and stops later packages from starting; **正在取消** remains visible until the executor finishes cleanup. Completed results and reported usage remain in history. Cancelling cannot undo charges already incurred or changes already integrated. Closing the panel does not cancel a run; reopening it in the same browser session can reconnect while the Host retains that job. Host restarts clear these in-memory jobs; durably saved package receipts and budget reservations remain. A confirmed dead execution owner is marked `interrupted`, without automatically resuming calls or releasing its hold. Preview, progress and cancellation requests stop waiting after 15 seconds. Progress reads retry against the same job; an unacknowledged cancellation can be retried explicitly. A transport timeout does not establish that the Host task stopped and never automatically resubmits `startRun`. Before retrying a recorded step, budget checks include that step and all unfinished downstream packages that will execute; reassignment uses the selected route estimate and unknown prices remain unknown. The [timeout recovery screenshot](docs/assets/workbench-run-timeout.png) is an offline simulation. History shows active and interrupted budget reservations separately from actual spending. Runs with a reservation cannot be rerun or reassigned. If a Host crash or checkpoint failure leaves a reservation, first inspect the original task, retained worktree and provider bill; this release has no manual reconciliation/release control. Do not delete state to make the capacity appear free. Changing task text, planning mode, profiles, directory or relevant settings invalidates the prior recommendation. Changing execution inputs also discards the pending or completed preview, so execution requires a new preview of the current request. Previewing execution uses current Host state and can differ from a previous local plan. Example task: ```text Review this project and prepare an implementation plan. 1. Map the entry points and identify the main UI workflows. 2. Review the interface at wide and narrow widths; list layout problems. 3. Check the execution and billing boundaries. 4. Combine the findings into a prioritized change list with verification steps. ``` The router plans and delegates text/code tasks. It does not itself render videos, generate artwork or control creative applications. ## Architecture and execution contracts The Host owns route discovery, settings, approvals, workspace validation, process launching and the persistent ledger. The React client requests previews and renders Host results. Planning, managed execution and installation requests accept fixed tool IDs and typed fields rather than arbitrary shell commands, executable paths, installer packages or download URLs. The same remote namespace separately exposes an explicitly confirmed interactive terminal, which accepts arbitrary user input under current-user permissions. ```mermaid flowchart TD UI[Workbench or Harness session] --> PLAN[Local planner and route profiles] PLAN --> PRE[Host preflight and confirmation] PRE --> ROUTED[Routed read-only executor] PRE --> TEAM[Official CLI team executor] ROUTED --> CLI[Supported headless CLI] ROUTED --> API[Harness model API] TEAM --> MODE{Permission mode} MODE -->|read-only| SANDBOX[Harness sandbox] MODE -->|workspace-write| WT[Isolated worktree] WT --> ENV{Explicit execution environment} ENV --> SANDBOX[Harness sandbox] ENV --> NATIVE[Normal vendor CLI environment] SANDBOX --> PROCESS[Official CLI process] NATIVE --> PROCESS PROCESS -->|editable success| PATCH[Baseline checks and patch integration] PROCESS --> LEDGER CLI --> LEDGER[Results, identity, usage and cost ledger] API --> LEDGER PATCH --> LEDGER ``` | Path | Selection and permissions | Failure/fallback behavior | | --- | --- | --- | | Routed execution | `model_router_execute` / workbench `executor: "routed"`; read-only; CLI or Harness model API according to execution/billing policy. | An eligible API fallback can follow the configured subscription policy. | | Official CLI, Harness environment | Single-tool `model_router_tool_run` or team execution; only currently supported/ready CLI modes; Host sandbox required. | Missing confinement or readiness blocks launch. No automatic API fallback. | | Official CLI, normal environment | Only editable official teams: `official-team + workspace-write + cli-native`; separate user confirmation. | Runs under current user permissions with `sandboxEnforcement: "none"`. No automatic environment switch or API fallback. | **Discovery is not execution acceptance.** Installed version, trusted launch entry, login status, supported permission mode, network connectivity and model entitlement are different checks. A CLI working in an interactive terminal can still be unavailable in a restricted task: the adapter, platform, sandbox and selected installation must all match. ### Workbench RPC The authenticated Host remote is `ctx.remote.modelRouterOfficialTools`, defined in [official-tools-remote.mjs](.dsh-plugin/shared/official-tools-remote.mjs). It is an internal mounted-client interface, not a standalone public HTTP API. A preview request has this shape: ```json { "task": "Analyze this repository's logging, implement a small improvement, and verify it.", "executor": "official-team", "planMode": "team", "executionMode": "workspace-write", "executionEnvironment": "cli-native", "workspace": "C:/work/example-repository", "budgetUsd": 1, "preset": "balanced" } ``` Replace the workspace with an existing clean Git root. Call `previewRun(request)`, decode its response with the client's `unwrapRemote` helper, show the plan and `reasons`, and stop if blocked. Preview does not call a model or create a worktree; entry/version/integrity checks may access the network. Only after the user accepts every current reason may the client call `startRun({ ...request, confirmedReasons: preview.reasons.map(r => r.code) })`. Native editing normally requires `workspace-write` and `unsandboxed`; an exceeded budget adds `over-budget`. Do not hardcode this list or populate it without consent. `startRun` replans and repeats preflight; it does not consume a frozen preview token. New confirmation requirements return `needs-confirmation` with `missing` and updated reasons. Changing task, mode, workspace or profiles requires a fresh preview. Workbench requests use saved route `cliModel` mappings; temporary `cliModelsJson` bindings belong to the session tool below. An accepted `startRun` returns a job snapshot with `jobId`, `status` and `progress` before execution finishes. Poll `runStatus({ jobId })`; request cancellation with `cancelRun({ jobId })`. Job states are `running`, `cancelling`, `completed`, `cancelled` or `failed`. A terminal snapshot's `result` contains the final workbench response and ledger `runId` when saved. `completed` means the worker settled; inspect `result.status` for the actual task outcome. Progress contains package identities and states, not answer text. A failed poll does not establish that execution stopped, and clients must not retry `startRun` automatically. ## Session tools Ask an official Harness session to invoke these tools. Configure the session workspace before tasks that access local files. | Tool | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `model_router_routes` | List configured routes; does not verify account/network availability. | | `model_router_plan` | Generate a local `single` or `team` plan. | | `model_router_consult` | Ask one configured model for a live second opinion via the model API. | | `model_router_execute` | Execute a read-only routed plan, or one explicit `provider`/`model`, with recorded results. | | `model_router_tools` / `model_router_health` | Inspect installation/readiness or version/login/billing health. | | `model_router_tool_install` | Install one fixed registry tool from its official source. | | `model_router_tool_run` | Run one supported CLI in `read-only` or approved `workspace-write` mode. | | `model_router_team_execute` | Replan among currently executable CLI routes, then run work packages sequentially. | | `model_router_rerun_step` | Rerun a failed step and its unfinished dependents, resume eligible editable teams, or repeat a failed single-tool run. | | `model_router_rate` | Record `up`, `down` or `clear` for one stored result. | Session commands are `/router `, `/tools`, and `/tools install|cancel `. A local planning request: ```json {"task":"Review the architecture and prepare a verification checklist","mode":"team","budgetUsd":10} ``` A read-only single-tool request: ```json {"tool":"codex","task":"Inspect the repository and list UI layout issues; do not edit files","mode":"read-only"} ``` An editable native-team request to `model_router_team_execute`: ```json { "task": "1. Analyze the logging module and propose a small improvement. 2. Implement it and report verification results.", "mode": "workspace-write", "executionEnvironment": "cli-native", "budgetUsd": 1 } ``` The session supplies its authorized workspace; configure it as an editable clean Git root first. The tool's approval hook requests the required confirmations. Session tool arguments use `mode`, not the workbench's `executionMode`, and do not accept `workspace`, `executor` or `planMode`. For temporary model binding, `cliModelsJson` is a JSON-encoded **string**, for example `"{\"claude-code\":\"\"}"`; replace the placeholder with a model accepted by that installation. This mapping does not force the planner to select that tool. Supply `provider` and `model` together when selecting an exact catalog route. All CLIs retain their own configured model by default; a catalog recommendation is never automatically passed as a CLI model argument. To switch explicitly, save a verified **官方 CLI 模型名** in the route profile, pass `cliModel` for one tool call, or use team `cliModelsJson`. Team bindings prefer a package id, then a tool id, then the saved route mapping. ZCode uses its own default and cannot switch model per call. History records the recommendation, requested CLI name and reported actual model separately; a request is not proof of the model used. Check vendor records when no actual model is reported. The CLI team runner is the plugin's own sequential dependency executor. It does not control the model selection or lifecycle of Harness's built-in Agent Teams. ## Official tools and execution modes | Registry id | Tool | Managed single-tool/team modes | | --- | --- | --- | | `kimi-code` | Kimi Code | Approved `workspace-write` | | `claude-code` | Claude Code | Windows: `read-only`, approved `workspace-write` | | `codex` | Codex CLI | Windows: Harness `read-only`; explicit native editable team supports `workspace-write` | | `minimax-code` | MiniMax Code | Approved `workspace-write` | | `mimo-code` | MiMo Code | Windows: `read-only`, approved `workspace-write` | | `grok-build` | Grok Build | Windows: `read-only`, approved `workspace-write` | | `gemini` | Gemini CLI | Routed headless adapter; not the managed single-tool/team runner | | `opencode` | OpenCode | Install, probe and login check; no verified restricted execution entry yet | | `stepcode` | Step Code | Install, probe and login check; no verified restricted execution entry yet | | `hermes` | Hermes Agent | Official Windows/POSIX installer, version checks and interactive terminal; authenticate with `hermes auth`; no verified managed runner | | `pi` | Pi | Official npm/pnpm package and interactive terminal; enter `/login` inside Pi; no verified managed runner | | `zcode` | ZCode CLI | Standalone TUI and approved `workspace-write` when its runtime entry is ready | | `dsh-tui` | [dsh-TUI](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI) | The DeepSeek tool: Harness terminal UI (pixel whale, live state, session manager). npm/pnpm install, probe and terminal; DeepSeek providers name it as their channel, while calls keep using the model directory API until a verified headless adapter exists | Hermes uses its [official source installer](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/installation) in non-interactive mode, then you run `hermes auth`. A configured shared root places its source in `/hermes-agent`; the plugin binds that checkout's `.hermes/bin` launcher and refuses a different old global copy. Existing configuration, login and history stay in their original Hermes home. Without a shared root, vendor defaults remain in use. The installer may refresh its global convenience command to the selected checkout. Uninstall source installs through `hermes uninstall`. Pi uses [`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/main/packages/coding-agent) through npm/pnpm with `--ignore-scripts` and requires Node.js 22.19 or later. Start `pi`, then enter `/login`. Both tools keep login status unknown until confirmed in their own interface; the plugin does not read their credentials. Installers use fixed official npm packages at each vendor's `@latest`, the vendor's own installer script, or the [community-maintained ZCode CLI release](https://github.com/Alice-Marx/zcode-cli) archive verified with its published SHA-256. An installation newer than the reported latest is not downgraded. Latest-version lookups are cached for about 12 hours; unavailable lookups leave the version unknown. New vendor releases are not automatically validated by this project. ZCode CLI is an independent Node.js distribution extracted from ZCode, not an official Z.AI release; it requires Node 2
