evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# wenlo-bot ### 把 DeepSeek Harness 变成一支数字员工团队 在频道里说一句任务，负责人拆解、派给员工执行，最后把成果交到你手上。
员工各自挂模型和 skill，有记忆，能被 @、能私信，干完的流程还能沉淀成新技能。 [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/wenlo/wenlo-bot?include_prereleases&label=release&color=111111)](https://github.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/releases) [![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.1--rc.5-111111)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-111111)](LICENSE) **[下载](https://github.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/releases)**  ·  **[快速开始](#快速开始)**  ·  **[功能](#功能)**  ·  **[扩展 API](docs/extension-api.md)**

## 适合谁 DSH 默认是一个人对一个会话。任务一复杂，你就得自己拆步骤、换会话、来回粘贴上下文。wenlo-bot 在 DSH 里加了一层团队协作： - 你只对**负责人**说需求，它负责拆解、派工、催进度和汇总。 - 每个**员工**是一份固定的职责：自己的模型、自己的 skill、自己的记忆，换任务不用重新交代。 - 过程留在**线程**里，结果落成**成果文件**，有版本、能定稿、能下载。 如果你常让 AI 做多步骤的活（调研加写作、资料整理加出稿、分析加汇报），它适合你。如果你只是偶尔问一两句，DSH 自带的会话就够了。 ## 快速开始 先安装 DSH（需 `0.2.1-rc.5` 版本），并配置至少一个可用模型。wenlo-bot 直接复用 DSH 里注册的模型与凭据，不需要另建账户。 **1. 添加插件市场。** 两个包均已发布在 npm，通过本仓库提供的索引源安装。在 DSH 的 **插件** 页打开 **实验性插件** → **更多**，启用「自定义插件市场」，切到 **发现** 标签，点击 **添加索引源**，填入： ```text https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/main/market/index.json ``` **2. 安装。** 在列表里安装 **Wenlo Bot** 和 **Wenlo Bot 界面**，两个包必须保持同一版本。看到下次启动生效的提示后，完全退出 DSH 再重新打开。 若不方便使用市场，也可以从 [Releases](https://github.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/releases) 下载两个 `.tgz` 手动安装，注意先装后端、再装界面： | 文件 | 作用 | |---|---| | `wenlo-wenlo-bot-<版本>.tgz` | 后端：频道、员工、派工、记忆、技能 | | `wenlo-wenlo-bot-ui-<版本>.tgz` | 界面：工作台页面 | DSH 桌面版：在侧栏进入 **插件** → **添加插件**，在地址栏填入 `.tgz` 的绝对路径并启用。 DSH Web 版（需要 Node.js 22.19 以上）： ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 plugin --profile web add npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 plugin --profile web add npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 web ``` 命令行安装到其他 profile 时，把 `web` 换成目标 profile 即可。桌面版的 `desktop` profile 只能由其自身修改：先完全退出桌面版，再用安装目录下的 `resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh` 执行相同命令。 ### 更新 升级 DSH 或拉取新源码都不会自动更新插件，两个包需要同时更新到同一版本。通过市场更新时，有新版会自动提示，更新后完全退出并重新打开 DSH 即可；DSH 升级后若旧版插件不再兼容，市场会将其标为不兼容，并推荐适配新版 DSH 的版本。 若不方便使用市场，可以从 [Releases](https://github.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/releases) 下载最新版的两个 tgz 手动更新。桌面版用户在「插件」页用新版 tgz 更新同名插件，两个包都更新完后完全退出并重开 DSH；Web / CLI 用户先停止运行中的实例，再在原 profile 重新安装两个包： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add <新版后端tgz绝对路径> <新版界面tgz绝对路径> ``` 把命令里的 `web` 换成原来使用的 profile，再按原方式启动 DSH。更新时无需先卸载插件；只要保留原来的 `DSH_HOME`、profile 和数据目录，员工、频道、会话与材料都会继续沿用。 本仓库维护通用 Bot 核心与公开扩展 API。私有工作台通过扩展 API 接入专属页面和预览卡片，按需独立更新；白标发行壳暂时冻结。 **3. 开工。** 打开工作台，首次启动已经有一个「任务大厅」频道和三名员工：负责人、分析、执行。直接在任务大厅里描述任务即可；要调整分工，在员工管理里改职责、模型和 skill，或者添加新员工。 ## 怎么运作 ```mermaid flowchart LR U([你]) -- 频道里发任务 --> L[负责人] L -- 拆解与派工 --> A[员工 A
模型 + skill] L -- 拆解与派工 --> B[员工 B
模型 + skill] A -- 回报与交接 --> L B -- 回报与交接 --> L L -- 汇总 --> D[(成果文件)] D --> U U -. "@员工 / 私信 / 线程追问" .-> A ``` 每名员工背后都是一个 DSH 原生会话，用 DSH 的工具和模型执行。负责人只调度，不替员工干活；你随时可以绕过负责人，直接 @ 某名员工或私信它。 ## 功能 ### 频道与负责人派工 频道是一个工作场所，由负责人接任务。负责人按依赖拆步骤，派给合适的员工，等上一步的产出到位再交给下一步；缺资料或需要人工确认时会停下来问你，不拿通用方案冒充完成。执行中的任务可以随时取消，中断的任务可以继续。 ### 线程、@ 和私信 任何一条消息都能展开成线程继续追问，不打乱频道主线。输入 `@` 从列表里挑员工，它会直接回你。私信是你和单个员工的独立对话，历史单独保存。
### 员工：模型、skill、记忆 员工有名字、职责、模型和 skill。模型从 DSH 已注册的 provider 里选，留空时用全局默认模型。skill 来自 DSH 官方 skills registry，也可以用自己写的。 记忆分三层：全局、频道、员工。你可以写下长期交代（比如「文案用短句，不用夸张承诺」），员工在之后的任务里照做；记忆也能随时查看、修改和删除。 ### 材料与成果 你上传的文件是材料，员工交出的文件是成果。成果保留全部版本，可以标为最终版、在线打开或下载。工具写出的文件、对话里的附件和成果在同一个文件视图里按来源区分。 ### 把做过的流程沉淀成技能 一套流程跑顺之后，负责人可以把它整理成技能草稿。草稿进入你的审核：可以直接编辑，每次保存会重算检查提示，有阻止项时不能安装；不满意就写上意见退回给负责人重整。审核通过后一键安装并绑定到员工，下次同类任务直接复用。 ### 作业画布 用画布查看当前有哪些员工在干活、各自在哪一步、哪些已完成或失败，点开节点能看到对应的会话和任务。 ### 界面与主题 两种布局：Discord 风格（频道分区，消息靠左）和微信风格（会话列表，消息左右排列）。明暗可以跟随系统，也可以固定浅色或深色。界面支持中文和英文，默认跟随浏览器语言，可以在设置里切换。 员工头像默认是圆形眼睛，也可以换成复古终端屏；终端屏风格下，员工执行时可以显示哈希代码、二进制流或命令行滚屏特效。 ### 备份 一键把工作台数据和原生会话备份到本机，包括材料、全部成果版本、对话和执行目录。开始前需要等任务结束，备份期间工作台的变更会排队等待。DSH 凭据库不在备份里，换机器后需要重新配置 Key。备份可能包含你输入过的敏感内容，不要公开。 ## 数据与隐私 所有数据留在你自己的电脑上：工作台数据在 DSH 数据目录下的 `workbench/`，员工会话由 DSH 管理。wenlo-bot 没有使用统计上报，不保存模型凭据，模型请求只发往你在 DSH 里配置的 provider。 唯一的例外是联网搜索结果的站点图标：界面会按结果的域名向 Google favicon 服务（`www.google.com/s2/favicons`）请求图标，Google 能看到这些域名和你的 IP；请求失败时回退为字母图标。 ## 扩展 wenlo-bot 核心只提供通用的协作能力，不附带行业目录或制作流程。行业模板、专用页面和工具可以做成独立扩展：host 侧通过 Cordis 服务注册路由、模板和技能来源，UI 侧通过插座注册页面、导航和设置项。扩展只依赖公开类型入口 `@wenlo/wenlo-bot/extension` 和 `@wenlo/wenlo-bot-ui/extension`。 详见 [扩展 API](docs/extension-api.md)。 ## 开发 项目用 pnpm workspace 管理，包含两个包： | 包 | 目录 | 形态 | |---|---|---| | `@wenlo/wenlo-bot` | [`workbench-host`](workbench-host) | Cordis host 插件 | | `@wenlo/wenlo-bot-ui` | [`workbench-ui`](workbench-ui) | `dsh.client` web 插件 | 环境要求 Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`、pnpm >= 9，与 DSH 宿主一致。 ```sh pnpm install pnpm -r typecheck pnpm -r test pnpm -r build ``` 启动独立浏览器开发版： ```sh pnpm dev [--port 3099] ``` 数据保存在当前工作树 `tmp/dev-web/`，前端改动由 HMR 热更新，后端改动自动热重载。首次启动如需注入本地模型配置，可设置环境变量 `WENLO_BOT_DEV_PROFILE_PATCH` 指向 cordis patch 文件；未设置时保持宿主默认，可在界面中配置模型。 装包前必须先构建，发布文件以各包 `files` 白名单为准。依赖钉版、运行时契约和贡献规范见 [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)。提交信息使用 conventional 前缀（`feat:`、`fix:`、`chore:`）。 ## 致谢 - [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)：wenlo-bot 构建在 DSH 插件系统之上，`build-support/` 来自 DSH 上游。 - [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)：内置 skill `document-to-action-items` 改编自其中的实现。 - [React Flow](https://reactflow.dev)：作业画布。 ## 许可证 [MIT](LICENSE)。按「原样」提供，不附带任何担保。第三方代码的来源与许可见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。 ## 免责声明 wenlo-bot 是独立的社区项目，**不是 DeepSeek 官方产品**，与 DeepSeek 没有隶属、背书或赞助关系。「DeepSeek」「DeepSeek Harness」等名称归各自所有者，这里只用来说明本插件运行在什么平台上。 员工使用你自己的模型额度，并会按任务需要读写文件、执行命令。重要操作请自己核对。

# wenlo-bot ### 把 DeepSeek Harness 变成一支数字员工团队 在频道里说一句任务，负责人拆解、派给员工执行，最后把成果交到你手上。
员工各自挂模型和 skill，有记忆，能被 @、能私信，干完的流程还能沉淀成新技能。 [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/wenlo/wenlo-bot?include_prereleases&label=release&color=111111)](https://github.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/releases) [![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.1--rc.5-111111)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-111111)](LICENSE) **[下载](https://github.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/releases)**  ·  **[快速开始](#快速开始)**  ·  **[功能](#功能)**  ·  **[扩展 API](docs/extension-api.md)**

## 适合谁 DSH 默认是一个人对一个会话。任务一复杂，你就得自己拆步骤、换会话、来回粘贴上下文。wenlo-bot 在 DSH 里加了一层团队协作： - 你只对**负责人**说需求，它负责拆解、派工、催进度和汇总。 - 每个**员工**是一份固定的职责：自己的模型、自己的 skill、自己的记忆，换任务不用重新交代。 - 过程留在**线程**里，结果落成**成果文件**，有版本、能定稿、能下载。 如果你常让 AI 做多步骤的活（调研加写作、资料整理加出稿、分析加汇报），它适合你。如果你只是偶尔问一两句，DSH 自带的会话就够了。 ## 快速开始 先安装 DSH（需 `0.2.1-rc.5` 版本），并配置至少一个可用模型。wenlo-bot 直接复用 DSH 里注册的模型与凭据，不需要另建账户。 **1. 添加插件市场。** 两个包均已发布在 npm，通过本仓库提供的索引源安装。在 DSH 的 **插件** 页打开 **实验性插件** → **更多**，启用「自定义插件市场」，切到 **发现** 标签，点击 **添加索引源**，填入： ```text https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/main/market/index.json ``` **2. 安装。** 在列表里安装 **Wenlo Bot** 和 **Wenlo Bot 界面**，两个包必须保持同一版本。看到下次启动生效的提示后，完全退出 DSH 再重新打开。 若不方便使用市场，也可以从 [Releases](https://github.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/releases) 下载两个 `.tgz` 手动安装，注意先装后端、再装界面： | 文件 | 作用 | |---|---| | `wenlo-wenlo-bot-<版本>.tgz` | 后端：频道、员工、派工、记忆、技能 | | `wenlo-wenlo-bot-ui-<版本>.tgz` | 界面：工作台页面 | DSH 桌面版：在侧栏进入 **插件** → **添加插件**，在地址栏填入 `.tgz` 的绝对路径并启用。 DSH Web 版（需要 Node.js 22.19 以上）： ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 plugin --profile web add npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 plugin --profile web add npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 web ``` 命令行安装到其他 profile 时，把 `web` 换成目标 profile 即可。桌面版的 `desktop` profile 只能由其自身修改：先完全退出桌面版，再用安装目录下的 `resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh` 执行相同命令。 ### 更新 升级 DSH 或拉取新源码都不会自动更新插件，两个包需要同时更新到同一版本。通过市场更新时，有新版会自动提示，更新后完全退出并重新打开 DSH 即可；DSH 升级后若旧版插件不再兼容，市场会将其标为不兼容，并推荐适配新版 DSH 的版本。 若不方便使用市场，可以从 [Releases](https://github.com/wenlo/wenlo-bot/releases) 下载最新版的两个 tgz 手动更新。桌面版用户在「插件」页用新版 tgz 更新同名插件，两个包都更新完后完全退出并重开 DSH；Web / CLI 用户先停止运行中的实例，再在原 profile 重新安装两个包： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add <新版后端tgz绝对路径> <新版界面tgz绝对路径> ``` 把命令里的 `web` 换成原来使用的 profile，再按原方式启动 DSH。更新时无需先卸载插件；只要保留原来的 `DSH_HOME`、profile 和数据目录，员工、频道、会话与材料都会继续沿用。 本仓库维护通用 Bot 核心与公开扩展 API。私有工作台通过扩展 API 接入专属页面和预览卡片，按需独立更新；白标发行壳暂时冻结。 **3. 开工。** 打开工作台，首次启动已经有一个「任务大厅」频道和三名员工：负责人、分析、执行。直接在任务大厅里描述任务即可；要调整分工，在员工管理里改职责、模型和 skill，或者添加新员工。 ## 怎么运作 ```mermaid flowchart LR U([你]) -- 频道里发任务 --> L[负责人] L -- 拆解与派工 --> A[员工 A
模型 + skill] L -- 拆解与派工 --> B[员工 B
模型 + skill] A -- 回报与交接 --> L B -- 回报与交接 --> L L -- 汇总 --> D[(成果文件)] D --> U U -. "@员工 / 私信 / 线程追问" .-> A ``` 每名员工背后都是一个 DSH 原生会话，用 DSH 的工具和模型执行。负责人只调度，不替员工干活；你随时可以绕过负责人，直接 @ 某名员工或私信它。 ## 功能 ### 频道与负责人派工 频道是一个工作场所，由负责人接任务。负责人按依赖拆步骤，派给合适的员工，等上一步的产出到位再交给下一步；缺资料或需要人工确认时会停下来问你，不拿通用方案冒充完成。执行中的任务可以随时取消，中断的任务可以继续。 ### 线程、@ 和私信 任何一条消息都能展开成线程继续追问，不打乱频道主线。输入 `@` 从列表里挑员工，它会直接回你。私信是你和单个员工的独立对话，历史单独保存。
### 员工：模型、skill、记忆 员工有名字、职责、模型和 skill。模型从 DSH 已注册的 provider 里选，留空时用全局默认模型。skill 来自 DSH 官方 skills registry，也可以用自己写的。 记忆分三层：全局、频道、员工。你可以写下长期交代（比如「文案用短句，不用夸张承诺」），员工在之后的任务里照做；记忆也能随时查看、修改和删除。 ### 材料与成果 你上传的文件是材料，员工交出的文件是成果。成果保留全部版本，可以标为最终版、在线打开或下载。工具写出的文件、对话里的附件和成果在同一个文件视图里按来源区分。 ### 把做过的流程沉淀成技能 一套流程跑顺之后，负责人可以把它整理成技能草稿。草稿进入你的审核：可以直接编辑，每次保存会重算检查提示，有阻止项时不能安装；不满意就写上意见退回给负责人重整。审核通过后一键安装并绑定到员工，下次同类任务直接复用。 ### 作业画布 用画布查看当前有哪些员工在干活、各自在哪一步、哪些已完成或失败，点开节点能看到对应的会话和任务。 ### 界面与主题 两种布局：Discord 风格（频道分区，消息靠左）和微信风格（会话列表，消息左右排列）。明暗可以跟随系统，也可以固定浅色或深色。界面支持中文和英文，默认跟随浏览器语言，可以在设置里切换。 员工头像默认是圆形眼睛，也可以换成复古终端屏；终端屏风格下，员工执行时可以显示哈希代码、二进制流或命令行滚屏特效。 ### 备份 一键把工作台数据和原生会话备份到本机，包括材料、全部成果版本、对话和执行目录。开始前需要等任务结束，备份期间工作台的变更会排队等待。DSH 凭据库不在备份里，换机器后需要重新配置 Key。备份可能包含你输入过的敏感内容，不要公开。 ## 数据与隐私 所有数据留在你自己的电脑上：工作台数据在 DSH 数据目录下的 `workbench/`，员工会话由 DSH 管理。wenlo-bot 没有使用统计上报，不保存模型凭据，模型请求只发往你在 DSH 里配置的 provider。 唯一的例外是联网搜索结果的站点图标：界面会按结果的域名向 Google favicon 服务（`www.google.com/s2/favicons`）请求图标，Google 能看到这些域名和你的 IP；请求失败时回退为字母图标。 ## 扩展 wenlo-bot 核心只提供通用的协作能力，不附带行业目录或制作流程。行业模板、专用页面和工具可以做成独立扩展：host 侧通过 Cordis 服务注册路由、模板和技能来源，UI 侧通过插座注册页面、导航和设置项。扩展只依赖公开类型入口 `@wenlo/wenlo-bot/extension` 和 `@wenlo/wenlo-bot-ui/extension`。 详见 [扩展 API](docs/extension-api.md)。 ## 开发 项目用 pnpm workspace 管理，包含两个包： | 包 | 目录 | 形态 | |---|---|---| | `@wenlo/wenlo-bot` | [`workbench-host`](workbench-host) | Cordis host 插件 | | `@wenlo/wenlo-bot-ui` | [`workbench-ui`](workbench-ui) | `dsh.client` web 插件 | 环境要求 Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`、pnpm >= 9，与 DSH 宿主一致。 ```sh pnpm install pnpm -r typecheck pnpm -r test pnpm -r build ``` 启动独立浏览器开发版： ```sh pnpm dev [--port 3099] ``` 数据保存在当前工作树 `tmp/dev-web/`，前端改动由 HMR 热更新，后端改动自动热重载。首次启动如需注入本地模型配置，可设置环境变量 `WENLO_BOT_DEV_PROFILE_PATCH` 指向 cordis patch 文件；未设置时保持宿主默认，可在界面中配置模型。 装包前必须先构建，发布文件以各包 `files` 白名单为准。依赖钉版、运行时契约和贡献规范见 [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)。提交信息使用 conventional 前缀（`feat:`、`fix:`、`chore:`）。 ## 致谢 - [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)：wenlo-bot 构建在 DSH 插件系统之上，`build-support/` 来自 DSH 上游。 - [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)：内置 skill `document-to-action-items` 改编自其中的实现。 - [React Flow](https://reactflow.dev)：作业画布。 ## 许可证 [MIT](LICENSE)。按「原样」提供，不附带任何担保。第三方代码的来源与许可见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。 ## 免责声明 wenlo-bot 是独立的社区项目，**不是 DeepSeek 官方产品**，与 DeepSeek 没有隶属、背书或赞助关系。「DeepSeek」「DeepSeek Harness」等名称归各自所有者，这里只用来说明本插件运行在什么平台上。 员工使用你自己的模型额度，并会按任务需要读写文件、执行命令。重要操作请自己核对。

                           this repository does not carry; the tracked manifest

is listed in section 2, that file's own terms govern it.


2. Bundled third-party material
-------------------------------

2.1 Font — none redistributed (removed 2026-10-31)
    Earlier versions bundled Great Vibes, SIL Open Font License 1.1, at
    build/great-vibes-latin.woff2 together with its licence text at
    build/great-vibes-OFL.txt. Both files were removed on 2026-10-31 with the
    rest of the theme's font changes, so no OFL material ships here any more and
    none of the OFL conditions attach to this package. No other font is
    redistributed either: every family named in src/theme.css (Bahnschrift, DIN
    Alternate, DIN Next, Eurostile Extended, Helvetica Neue, Inter, Arial,
    sans-serif) is referenced by name only and is never shipped.

2.2 Brand marks — build/brand-mark.png, build/brand-mark-dark.png,
    build/brand-mark.jpg
    CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Credits and the list of changes we made are in NOTICE
    section 2. Three consequences you must respect:

      BY — keep the credits. Attribution goes to the character's author 上善无形
           (original character 溟月), the DeepSeek-element second pass by
           ZipZipPipe (GPT Image 2), and the refined repair by QYQCAMIAO.
      NC — no commercial use. Ads, sponsorship, paid distribution and paid
           products all count, whether or not you charge for this package.
      SA — share alike. brand-mark-dark.png is a derivative (see NOTICE), and any
           adaptation or derivative you distribute must carry the same licence.

2.3 Wallpapers — NOT distributed, hotlinked
    Since 2026-10-09 (D79) this repository distributes no wallpaper
    image, and since D81 the tracked manifest names the pictures by URL rather than
    leaving the layer empty. Both background images are third-party artwork, not
    ours, and we grant no licence in them. What this repository holds is an address
    and a credit, in two files:

      build/wallpapers.json      TRACKED. Two entries, each with a `direct:` URL
                                 and the `page:` its credit belongs on. The build
                                 emits url("https://…"), so a theme built from
                                 this file paints two pictures the browser fetches,
                                 at paint time, from the host each entry names. No
                                 image bytes travel with it, and an offline machine
                                 simply has no background.
      out/wallpapers.local.json  LOCAL, ignored by git. The same shape with
                                 `dataUrl:` entries; when it exists the build
                                 embeds those local copies instead, which is how
                                 the maintainer's own machine keeps its look.
                                 `--public` ignores it.
      client.js                  GENERATED, ignored by git. `npm run selfcheck`
                                 asserts that the tracked manifest carries no
                                 `dataUrl:` (wall.6) and that a bundle built from
                                 it resolves every `direct:` URL (wall.8). An empty
                                 manifest is still legal: it publishes
                                 `--cp-pick-light: none; --cp-pick-dark: none;`.

    Provenance, recorded because it is the maintainer's own record and because it
    is what a takedown request would be about:

      og33jl — wallhaven.cc/w/og33jl, 2560x1440, credited there to the artist YOTA
               SAKI; the entry's source link is pixiv.net/en/artworks/133258822.
               Uploaded to wallhaven by "Elisban". Not licensed to us.
      eva01city — haowallpaper.com/homeViewLook/18703364605463936, 1100x775, the
                  light-mode default. The page credits no artist, only its
                  uploader; the same artwork also circulates on wallhaven as
                  x85po3, uploaded there by "BachoWilson". haowallpaper serves this
                  preview to anonymous visitors, so the 3066x2160 original — which
                  the maintainer holds, and which this file does not point at — is
                  behind a signed-in download. Not licensed to us.

    We have no permission from either artist. If you are one of them and want the
    entry gone, ask and it will be dropped from the manifest. See README, "Fan work
    and attribution", which also keeps the maintainer's standing notice about images
    taken from the web.


3. What comes from where
------------------------

  index.js, src/, tools/, docs/, cordis.patch.yml ... MIT (section 1)
  client.js ......................................... MIT (generated from src/, not tracked)
  build/brand-mark*.png, build/brand-mark.jpg ....... CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (2.2)
  the wallpaper pair ................................ NOT distributed, hotlinked (2.3)

Vendored code. Two files are byte-for-byte copies of code from other plugins, not
written for this theme:

  build/plugin-toggle.js ....... dsh-disable-unofficial-plugins, MIT
                                 https://github.com/WhatCannotBeSaid/dsh-disable-unofficial-plugins
  build/session-eva-status.js .. dsh-session-eva-status v0.1.0, MIT
                                 https://github.com/WhatCannotBeSaid/dsh-session-eva-status

Both upstreams are MIT, whose notice has to travel with copies and substantial
portions. NOTICE section 3 carries both entries, and the MIT text with its
copyright line is section 1 of this file. The two files are also inlined into the
generated client.js, so that notice belongs with the bundle and not only with the
two source files. Keep it if you redistribute either file or the bundle.

The CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 legal text for section 2.2 ships with this repository as
LICENSE-CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.txt; the canonical copy is
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/legalcode

No `EVA`, `NERV`, `Evangelion` or Arknights artwork owned by khara, inc. or
Hypergryph is distributed in this package. The only images this repository
carries are the brand marks in 2.2 — both wallpapers are absent as bytes by
construction (2.3), which keeps only their addresses and their credits. The theme
is an unofficial, non-commercial fan work, published under
khara's fan-work guideline (https://www.khara.co.jp/guideline/), which permits
non-commercial fan works and licenses neither the characters nor the brand. See
README, "Fan work and attribution".

# QUASAR — dsh-quasar-theme

[![Licence: MIT + CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT%20%2B%20CC--BY--NC--SA%204.0-yellow.svg)](#licence)

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**QUASAR** is a space-themed skin for **DeepSeek Harness**: an ink black hole in
the sidebar brand row, a live accretion disk behind the app, and one removable
override layer of 53 measured tokens whose translucent surfaces are solved
against a contrast budget rather than picked by eye.

The name is the one the interface has carried all along — the sidebar reads
`QUASAR CORE` — and the package now follows it: `dsh-quasar-theme`. A quasar is a
black hole with an accretion disk and a jet, which is what the canvas layer
draws. Until 2026-11-04 the package was called `dsh-universe-theme`; saved pins
and popover state migrate on first read (see [What it is](#what-it-is)).

**This repository ships no background picture.** The paint layer is here, the
artwork is not — the tracked wallpaper manifest is empty, so a fresh clone draws
the documented no-art state and makes no third-party request.

![dsh-quasar-theme, dark](docs/preview-dark.jpg)
![dsh-quasar-theme, light](docs/preview-light.jpg)

Both captures are the current build, dark and light, at 1600×1000. The
conversation list is hidden in both; nothing else is edited.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with a web profile.
- Node.js >= 18 — only for the build and check tools. The theme itself runs in
  the browser.

## Install

From npm — a versioned tarball with the browser bundle already built in:

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-quasar-theme
```

Straight from the public repository, which tracks its default branch:

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:WhatCannotBeSaid/dsh-quasar-theme
```

The package carries a `prepare` script that runs exactly that build, so an
install straight from the Git URL produces the bundle before the package is
linked; the npm tarball ships `client.js` ready-made and runs no build. From a
local checkout or a clone of it:

```
npm run build                                   # writes the browser bundle
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:<path-to-this-checkout>
```

Run the build once after cloning: `client.js` is generated and deliberately not
tracked (see [Layout](#layout)). A plain `git clone` needs one build — `npm run
build`, or any `npm install` inside the checkout, which triggers `prepare`.

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the profile reconciles its bundle
stack against the installed package and mounts the theme. If it does not appear
after a restart, append `dsh-quasar-theme` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the
profile's `package.json` — a package that is merely a dependency is not mounted.

## Remove

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-quasar-theme
```

Drop the entry from `dsh.profile.bundles` too if you added it there.

## What it is

| | |
|---|---|
| Modes | Light and dark, one override layer each arm |
| Token layer | 53 measured overrides — 41 in the light arm, 12 in the dark arm |
| Translucent surfaces | Two tokens carry a veil alpha: 0.84 in light, 0.35 in dark. Input cards and menus sit at 0.30 |
| Wallpaper | **None.** The paint layer and its no-art state are here; no artwork ships, is hotlinked, or is fetched at paint time |
| Black hole | A canvas layer behind the app: a photon ring and shadow, a lensed accretion disk whose 24 patches have finite lifetimes and are sheared by their own differential orbit. Phenomenological, not an MHD solve |
| Brand mark | The ink black hole supplied for this theme, drawn at 28×28 inside the sidebar's 36×36 slot |
| Wordmark | `QUASAR` in Cinzel 700 (0.10em tracking) and a `CORE` chip in EB Garamond 500 / 12px, both embedded as data URLs |
| Composer row | The merged model control becomes two independent buttons — model and reasoning effort — each with its own popover, neither with a disclosure chevron |
| Also inside | A pin button on every workspace and session row; a session status rail; the four popovers that hang off the composer row centred on their triggers |
| Language | All user-facing text goes through the official locale service (zh / en) |

The theme installs one layer and can be removed as one. It ships **no settings
panel of its own** — the look is fixed, not a preference — and the only thing it
persists is the workspace pin set and the composer's collapsed-popover state,
under `quasar-theme/workspace-pins` and `quasar-theme/model-groups-collapsed`.
Both are read from their earlier `uni-theme/` keys once and rewritten under the
new name, so upgrading does not reset either. It does hide
and move a few official entries, so read
[What it changes in the interface](#what-it-changes-in-the-interface) before you
install it.

No boot animation, no non-official-plugin switch, no wallpaper picker: those were
part of the earlier build and are gone.

## What it changes in the interface

Removing the package takes the layer away again and every official element comes
back. In between, the theme **hides six official entries, rewrites the sidebar
identity line, replaces one page's heading, and reshapes the composer's control
row**. All of it is CSS plus a few client effects — the official DOM is never
rewritten.

### The brand row is three click zones

The sidebar brand row reads **[ink black hole] QUASAR CORE**; the official
wordmark and its whale glyph are hidden. It is one official button carrying three
zones, decided from the click's x coordinate at click time:

| Click | Opens | Because |
|---|---|---|
| the ink mark, left of `QUASAR` | the **plugin panel** | the nav's 「插件」 row is hidden, so this is its only door |
| the `QUASAR` text | a **new session** | official behaviour, unchanged |
| the `CORE` chip, right of the text | **Settings** | the 「设置」 launcher button is hidden, so this is the visible door to it |

The mark and the chip both drive hidden official controls programmatically: the
mark clicks the hidden 「插件」 row, the chip clicks the hidden Settings launcher.
When that launcher is absent the chip asks the host's shortcut registry instead.
Only the name's stretch is left alone, so the official new-session handler runs
there. Keyboard activation (Enter or Space on the focused button) and any click
held with a modifier key are left alone. Collapse the sidebar to a rail and there
is no brand button, so there are no zones either.

Both embedded faces are SIL OFL 1.1, latin subset, travelling inside `client.js`
as data URLs, so the row looks the same on a machine that does not have them.
`build/fonts.json` is the provenance record, and the build fails when a file's
byte count disagrees with it (Cinzel 15,184 B, EB Garamond 25,264 B).

### Hidden official entries

| Entry | Where | Way back |
|---|---|---|
| 「应用」/「编辑」 title-bar menu | desktop shell only; absent in a browser | none from inside the app: 关于 / 检查更新 / dsh 命令 / 退出应用 go with it. Quit is still on the tray menu |
| the second 「新会话」 button | sidebar, below the brand row | `QUASAR`, or `Ctrl+N` — it is a duplicate |
| the 「插件」 nav row | sidebar | click the ink mark |
| 「设置」 row and its launcher button | sidebar | click the `CORE` chip, or `Ctrl+,` |
| 「收起侧栏」 button | left sidebar only; the right sidebar's stays visible | the collapse command itself is untouched |
| the session list's bottom fade | sidebar | it only dimmed the last row |
| the account card (only while the DeepSeek account plugin is enabled) | sidebar, in the Settings slot | removed outright, with no gap left where it stood; the chip still opens Settings |

Where a way back names a keyboard shortcut, that is the desktop default — `Ctrl+N`
for a new session, `Ctrl+,` for settings, both of them the official ones,
unchanged by this theme. The web build binds the same two commands to `Ctrl+Alt+N`
and `Ctrl+Alt+,`.

Nothing else in the sidebar moves. The workspace and session list keeps the
official `flex: 1` scrolling area, and the bottom area still shows whatever a
third-party plugin registers into `sidebar.footer.action`, in the position the
host gives it.

### The nav area sits under the title bar (desktop shell only)

The first nav button is level with the 对话 / 轨迹 tab row of the main area instead
of sitting below it, and the Settings row moves underneath the nav instead of
above it. That is the one visible reordering in the sidebar, and it applies to the
desktop shell only — the browser build has no title-bar strip to align to, so its
layout stays the one the host draws.

### The new session page (hero)

That page is the composer and nothing else. Three things are gone, on that page
only: the headline and its fixed German line, the 「预览版」/ “Preview” badge, and
the whale logo above them. The whole row goes, not just its text: an empty flex
row still holds the HeroShell's gap, which reads as a stray blank band rather than
as the composer having moved up. With the row `display: none` the composer sits
where the headline used to be.

### The composer's control row

The row above Send belongs to the host; the theme reshapes it and splits one of
its controls.

- The official merged model control becomes **two buttons**: the model and the
  reasoning effort. Each has its own popover, and opening one closes the other;
  neither carries a disclosure chevron, because the open state is already the
  trigger's own highlight.
- On a narrow row both triggers become 28×28 icon buttons — same box, same ink as
  the add and dictation buttons beside them. A wide row keeps the text labels.
- The whole row shares one seam — 6px when it has room, 3px when it does not — so
  the controls read as one strip instead of drifting groups.
- The four official popovers that hang off that row — permission, session stats,
  token usage and the context meter — are centred on their triggers instead of
  left-aligned with them. The sidebar's own view-options menu is left where the
  host puts it.

### What the theme adds

- A **pin button** on every workspace and session row (置顶工作区 / Pin workspace,
  following the host's language). The pinned set lives in browser storage under
  `uni-theme/workspace-pins`; the order it produces is written through the host's
  own insert-before API, so it survives a restart — and, unlike the pin set, it
  also survives removing the theme.
- The **session status rail**: blue and breathing while a session waits for you
  (an approval, a question, a plan review), red while it is the one open in the
  main area, purple while it finished unread. A pinned row gets a rainbow title
  instead of a rail.
- The **accretion disk** behind the app: a black hole with a lensed disk, drawn on
  a canvas and shaded per cell. Patches are advected by their own orbit, so a patch
  is sheared into an arc instead of sliding as a block. It holds still for anyone
  who asked for reduced motion.
- A **continuous composer transition**: sending the first message of a session
  slides the composer card down as one move instead of fading it out and popping
  a new one in.

Settings themselves remain the official dialog. The single change there is that
the dim tint behind it is removed; the panel and click-outside-to-close are
untouched.

## Layout

```
index.js              host half — mounts, registers no route, plays nothing
client.js             GENERATED browser bundle. Not tracked; build it. Do not edit.
src/client.js         service and effect orchestration
src/theme.css         the token layer
src/tokens.json       the token layer's source of truth for the build
src/runtime/          glass, black hole, geodesic lens, pins, brand routing, panels
src/model-effort-picker.js  the composer's two model/effort controls
cordis.patch.yml      the bundle-patch mount declaration
build/                shipped assets: brand marks, the two OFL fonts, fonts.json
build/wallpapers.json the TRACKED wallpaper manifest — empty in this repository
tools/                build, self-check, token audit, tests
docs/                 design log, recon, audits, render reports
NOTICE                upstream licences and third-party credits
LICENSE               this package's layered licence
LICENSE-CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.txt  the CC licence text for the brand marks
```

`client.js` is generated from `src/` and carries a banner saying so. Edit `src/`
and run `npm run build`; the check gate fails if the two drift apart.

`build/wallpapers.json` is tracked and currently empty. An empty manifest is the
documented no-art state: the build publishes `--cp-pick-light: none; --cp-pick-dark:
none;` and the paint layer draws nothing. A `direct:` entry would make the build
emit `url("https://…")` and the browser fetch that host at paint time — nothing in
this repository does that today. `out/wallpapers.local.json` (git-ignored) can
carry `dataUrl:` entries for a local build; `--mode public` ignores it.

## Checks

```
npm run verify
```

Runs the development gates: syntax checks on both bundle halves, the behavioral and
build-contract tests in `tools/*.test.mjs`, the static self-check (113 assertions,
all green at this version), the 53-token audit, and an exact artifact/source
comparison. Build and check commands accept the same `--mode auto|public|local`.

Individual gates: `npm run build` (writes `client.js`), `npm run check` (compares
it against `src/` without writing), `npm run selfcheck`, `npm run audit`, `npm test`.

Release validation is `npm run verify:release -- --mode public --host-version
<exact-version>`. Fresh target-host evidence, collection time and input hashes are
required; old dumps without provenance yield a partial development audit, not
verified compatibility. `npm run measure:resources` measures local compression and
Node compilation, not browser performance. Publish from a clean isolated checkout
without `out/`, then validate the packed artifact's public mode.

See [S1–S10 implementation and acceptance record](docs/optimization-s1-s10.md)
for limitations and rollback.

## Licence

This package uses **tiered licensing**. Each licence applies only to the part it is
named against; none of them is an alternative licence for the whole repository.
Catalogue data (`build/*.json`) describes assets without licensing them. No
trademark rights are granted here.

| Part | Licence | What it asks of you |
|---|---|---|
| Our code — `index.js`, `src/`, `tools/`, `client.js` | MIT | Keep the copyright and licence notice. Commercial use of the code is fine. |
| Project text — this README, `docs/`, `NOTICE`, `LICENSE` | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | Credit, link the licence, note changes, keep it non-commercial, share alike. |
| Fonts — `build/cinzel-latin-700.woff2`, `build/eb-garamond-latin-500.woff2` | SIL OFL 1.1 | Keep the licence with the font; the texts ship beside them as `build/cinzel-OFL.txt` and `build/eb-garamond-OFL.txt`. |
| The earlier brand marks still in the tree — `build/whale-maid-small-monochrome-diagonal.svg`, `build/brand-mark*.png`, `build/brand-mark.jpg` | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | Same terms as the project text, and this is third-party artwork: see below. |

Because those third-party marks carry a non-commercial term and still ship in the
package, **the package as a whole may not be used commercially**. The MIT code on
its own is not restricted; drop the marks if you need a commercial-use build.

Full terms: [LICENSE](LICENSE). Upstream texts and per-file credits:
[NOTICE](NOTICE). The CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 legal text ships as
[LICENSE-CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.txt](LICENSE-CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.txt) and is also at
<https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/>.

## Third-party marks and credits

**Current brand mark.** `build/brand-mark-black-hole.png`, the ink black hole the
sidebar draws, was supplied for this theme. It is not character artwork and names
no third party.

**Earlier brand mark.** Character 溟月 by 上善无形 (original character,
<https://space.bilibili.com/4456176>). DeepSeek-elements second pass by ZipZipPipe
(GPT Image 2, <https://space.bilibili.com/4168597>). Refined repair by QYQCAMIAO.
Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — credit, non-commercial, share alike. The illustration
ships as the supplied SVG, `build/whale-maid-small-monochrome-diagonal.svg`, drawn
unmodified. The earlier cropped 256×256 PNGs stay in the tree for rollback only,

Copyright 2017 The EB Garamond Project Authors. Both SIL OFL 1.1, latin subset,

host at paint time.

**History.** Earlier versions of this package were an EVA-inspired theme with two

package was renamed from `dsh-universe-theme` to `dsh-quasar-theme` on 2026-11-04

# dsh-resume

The manifest in this folder is the one the compatibility sample audits. Its
`engines.dsh` range is the real one from `L3n3L/dsh-resume@0.1.3`:

```json
"engines": {
  "dsh": ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"
}
```

# dsh-plugin-toolkit

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dw/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![CI](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](LICENSE)


![dsh-plugin-toolkit](docs/card.png)

English · [中文](./README.zh.md)

Everything a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin needs between `init` and a version the market index accepts: scaffolding, a test harness for the client bundle, a way to see a change without restarting the app, and a release that does not depend on remembering fourteen steps.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel   # a plugin that already passes the checks
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .                          # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release --pr --merge              # tag, wait for npm, update the index, open and merge the PR
```

## The panel

![The Plugin doctor tab, on a plugin that fails two checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/panel.png)

The same checks, in the right sidebar: type a folder, an `owner/repo`, or a GitHub link, and it says which one would fail and why. Nothing is installed and nothing is written.

## Three paths

| You are… | Start with | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| writing your first plugin | [`init`](#1-write-a-plugin) | `doctor`, `fix`, `verify` |
| changing a panel that is already installed | [`dev`](#2-develop-a-panel) | `mount`, the testkit, `audit` |
| shipping a version | [`verify`](#3-ship-a-version) | `release`, `index` |

It also installs as a plugin. `dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit` puts a
**插件体检 / Plugin doctor** panel under the conversation and a tab in the right
sidebar. Give it a folder that holds a plugin's `package.json`, or just
`owner/repo` — or a repository name, which it searches GitHub for and lists the
candidates to pick from. It then runs the same checks `verify` runs and says
which one would break the install, with the reason on the line — the same
answers as the CLI, without leaving the app.

```
$ dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit
```

### 1. Write a plugin

[`init`](#start-from-a-plugin-that-already-passes) writes the files whose absence shows up as a failed first publish — `engines.dsh`, the patch file, a `files` list that ships the code, a client bundle, a test for it, and the CI that runs both. `doctor` then checks the same things without writing anything, and [`verify`](#prove-the-tarball-works-not-just-the-repository) checks the tarball instead of the working copy.

If a plugin already exists, `doctor --fix` turns the failing checks into a
repair plan. It names the file and the edit for every problem, writes nothing
until you add `--write`, and then runs the checks again. `fix --engines` is
still there when the host range is the only thing you need to change.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel
cd my-panel && npm install && npm test && npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest doctor .
```

### 2. Develop a panel

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) supplies the missing half, and [`dev`](#edit-a-plugin-that-is-already-installed) pushes a rebuilt bundle into the running app.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest mount ./client.js     # what a user would see, without the app
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

### 3. Ship a version

`verify` first (it is the only check that reads the tarball), then `release`, which tags, waits for the registry, writes the index entry with the publish time the registry reports, and — with `--pr --merge` — opens and merges the pull request.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release . --pr --merge
```

## What `verify` actually does

![Five steps, and the failure each one catches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/pipeline.svg)

The order matters. Packing first means the check reads the file list npm will publish, not the folder you have. Installing the tarball means the root export is imported the way the loader imports it. Mounting means the client bundle is actually executed, in jsdom, with a host that records what it registered.

Each step exists because a plugin once got past the step before it and still installed into nothing.

## Why this exists

Releasing one plugin fifteen times taught me three things the ecosystem's tooling does not cover:

1. **A version is not shipped when npm accepts it.** Registry propagation took two to eight minutes every time. `npm view` answered from a stale local cache, so I repeatedly believed a release had failed when it had not — and once believed it had succeeded when the market still could not see it.
2. **The market index is a second release, done by hand.** Each version needs an entry carrying `publishTimestamp` from the registry and `engines.dsh` from the manifest. Forget the range and the index validator rejects the PR with `Engines mismatch` — after the tag is already public.
3. **Reading a manifest is not the same as checking it.** A plugin can have a valid `package.json` and still be uninstallable: `files` that omit the entry the manifest points at, a bundle patch that does not exist, a README that never states the host range it declares.

The five failures behind these checks — a red dot with no panel, a row the host drops, an app that disables every plugin after one unguarded `apply()`, a tab nothing can open, and a checker that was wrong — are written up with their exact error text and how to reproduce each one: [Five plugins that installed and did nothing](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/blob/main/docs/why-it-exists.md).

### Four ways a plugin installs and still does nothing

Each of these shipped in a real version of this toolkit before the check below existed. A manifest check passes on all four.

| What you see | What it was | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The tab is a red dot and the panel never opens | `exports["."]` pointed at the CLI, so the loader's row had no plugin to apply | `root export` |
| The plugin is installed, the app never serves it | `dsh.client` declared, `exports["./client"]` missing — the host drops the row | `client declaration` |
| The app says the third-party plugin is unsupported and disables all of them | `apply()` read `ctx.webServer` without declaring it; cordis throws instead of returning `undefined` | `verify` (calls `apply` on a context that has no services) |
| The tab registers, and nothing in the UI opens it | `sidebarRightTabs.register()` registers a *type*; the sidebar lists what `tabs.guide()` returns | a testkit test, not `doctor` |

The first three are static: `doctor` and `verify` catch them without the app running. The fourth is a UI contract, so it needs the panel mounted and the registration inspected — that is what [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) is for.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer (the registry is read with `fetch`; no runtime dependencies)
- Git and `gh` on `PATH` for the steps that touch GitHub
- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0` — the version whose market index carries `engines.dsh`, which is what makes the range check meaningful
- For `testkit`: `jsdom`, `react` and `react-dom` as dev dependencies (`npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom`)

## Start from a plugin that already passes

```sh
$ npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel --title "My panel"
created 8 file(s) in /Users/you/my-panel
  .github/workflows/ci.yml
  .gitignore
  README.md
  client.js
  cordis.patch.yml
  index.js
  package.json
  test/panel.test.mjs

next: npm install && npm test && npm run doctor
```

What you get is not a snippet: it is a plugin whose `doctor` already passes (`engines.dsh`, the patch file, the `files` list), with a client bundle that registers a sidebar tab, a testkit test for it, and a CI workflow that runs both. `init` refuses a directory that is not empty unless you pass `--force`, and refuses a name npm would refuse — those are the two mistakes that cost the most time later.

## Where it lives

The checker is docked **under the conversation**, above the input bar: a single
row, collapsed by default. Open it and it carries the whole guide — who it is
for, how to use it, what each check means, and what it cannot tell you — plus
the folder field and the results. The same panel is also a **Plugin doctor** tab
in the right sidebar, for when the conversation is busy.

The panel speaks both languages and opens in Chinese; the 中文 / EN switch sits
in the dock's header row (and in the sidebar tab) and the choice is remembered.

Look at it without the app:

```sh
node scripts/preview.mjs /tmp/panel.html   # collapsed, open, with a result, and the tab
```

## Test a panel without a browser

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. `testkit` supplies the missing half: a DOM, the real React, and a host context that records what the panel registers.

```sh
npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom
```

```js
import { mountClient, createFetch } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({
  file: 'client.js',
  copy: { 'my-plugin': { title: 'My panel' } },
  fetch: createFetch({
    '/my-plugin/report': { body: { score: 71, noise: 3 } },
    '/my-plugin/apply': () => ({ status: 201, body: { score: 92 } }),
  }),
});

await panel.click('[data-testid="optimize"]');
console.assert(panel.text().includes('92'), 'the score on screen did not move');
console.assert(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent.includes('92'));
await panel.unmount();
```

`unmount()` is async: it lets React finish the work its own unmount schedules before the DOM goes away. Skipping the `await` surfaces as `ReferenceError: window is not defined` *after* the test has already passed, which is a confusing way to learn it.

What you get back: `text()`, `html()`, `query(selector)`, `must(selector)` (throws with the rendered HTML when it misses), `click(selector)`, `type(selector, value)`, `press(selector, key)`, `focus`, `attributes(selector)`, `snapshot(dir, name)` for a normalised DOM baseline, and `host` for assertions about what the bundle registered.

### Keep a visual baseline

The DOM is the baseline: normalising class order and whitespace gives a file that fails for the reasons a screenshot would — a lost label, a control that stopped rendering — and can be reviewed in a diff instead of by eye.

```js
import { expectSnapshot } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({ file: 'client.js' });
expectSnapshot(panel.html(), '__snapshots__', 'panel');   // throws with the element that moved
await panel.unmount();
```

First run writes nothing: it tells you to re-run with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, so a baseline is always a decision, never a side effect.

### Check what assistive tech sees

```js
panel.expectAria('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]', { label: 'Protection', selected: 'true' });
assert.match(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent, /Score moved 71 → 77/);
```

`expectAria()` compares the attributes a screen reader actually reads — `role`,
`label`, `live`, `selected`, `expanded`, `checked`, `pressed`, `disabled` — and
names the one that differs:

```
[aria-live="polite"]: expected aria text to be "9", but it is "0"
```

A missing attribute is reported as `nothing`, not as an empty string, because
those are different bugs. `panel.aria(selector)` returns the same object when you
want to assert on it yourself.

`must()` throws with the rendered markup when the selector misses, which is the difference between "the assertion failed" and "here is what the user actually got".

Every example below is a file in this repository, run by CI, and the output shown is the output it prints:

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs` | mount a real bundle, read the text, click, read it again |
| `node examples/route-stubs.mjs` | answer the routes a panel asks for, and assert on the requests |
| `node examples/baseline.mjs` | a DOM baseline compared on every run |
| `node examples/aria.mjs` | what assistive tech sees |

```sh
$ node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs
Demo panel Count 0 0
Demo panel Count 1 1
```

```sh
$ node examples/route-stubs.mjs
Score 71
asked for: 1 route(s), undeclared route answers 404
```

To look at a bundle by hand:

```sh
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js            # print the text a user would see
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js --html     # print the markup
```

That is how the AIignore panel was checked before release: the real bundle, mounted in Node, against a stubbed `/aiignore/*`:

```
$ npx dsh-plugin mount ../ai-context-doctor/plugin/client.js
AIignore No workspace yet Could not read the report …
```

## Put the badge on a plugin that passes

If `verify` passes on your plugin, this badge says so and links back here:

```md
[![checked with dsh-plugin-toolkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
```

It is a claim, not a decoration: add it only when `dsh-plugin verify .` exits 0.

## Start from the example

[`dsh-plugin-example`](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-example) is a ~70-line plugin: one sidebar tab, two languages, one behaviour test, CI that runs `verify` through the composite action. It is the shape this toolkit expects, so it is also the fastest way to see whether the toolkit fits your plugin. It is a GitHub template too: **Use this template** starts you on a plugin whose first publish already passes.

```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-example
```

## See what is installed, and what the app loaded

`doctor` checks one folder you name. The question that actually gets asked is
"why is my plugin not in the sidebar?", and the answer needs three things at once:
what is installed, whether each installed copy is valid, and which of them the
running app actually loaded.

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
dsh-aiignore           0.37.1    loaded       ok
demo-panel             0.3.0     not loaded   ok  — dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json does not list it, and the loader mounts only listed bundles
                                            fix: add "demo-panel" to dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json (or run `dsh plugin add demo-panel`), then restart the app

1 installed plugin(s) are not in the running app:
```

"Not loaded" has three different causes, and `audit` names the one that applies
instead of offering a blanket restart:

- **Not in `dsh.profile.bundles`.** `pnpm add` (or `npm install`) installs the
  package but does not tell the loader to mount it. Add the package name to
  `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`, or run
  `dsh plugin add <name>`, then restart the app.
- **No `dsh.bundle`.** The package declares `dsh` but no patch file to mount.
  Add `dsh.bundle.patch` to its `package.json` and ship the patch file, then
  reinstall.
- **Listed, but the app predates the install.** The profile is already correct;
  restart the app once to read the new list.

Advisories (`engines.dsh`, README Requirements) are counted apart from problems:
the market index needs them, the loader does not, so they should not bury a plugin
that is actually broken.

`audit` exits `1` when an installed plugin has a hard failure **or** when the
running app did not load at least one installed plugin, so CI can gate on a
profile where the app silently skipped a plugin. It exits `0` when every
installed plugin is loaded and valid. If no graph was read (`--host` omitted),
the loaded column is `?` and only hard failures change the exit code.

Without `--host` the loaded column is `?`, because guessing would be worse than
saying nothing. Only packages that declare a `dsh` field are audited — the rest of
`node_modules` is ordinary dependencies, and auditing those is noise.

## Edit a plugin that is already installed

The host already swaps a rebuilt bundle without a page reload: it watches each plugin's entry artifact and reports a `rebuilt` frame on `/plugins/events`. `dev` puts the new file where the host is looking, then **proves** the frame arrived instead of asking you to check by eye.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

![dsh-plugin dev printing the revision the app reported](docs/dev.gif)

*Recorded from a real run against the running app: the last line is the revision the app sent back on `/plugins/events`, not a message the tool printed on faith.*

```
demo-aiignore: /work/plugin/client.js -> ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-aiignore/client.js
initial: copied 163647 bytes at 1:18:43 AM
reloaded dsh-aiignore (rev e0c0230c4fc9)
watching /work/plugin
```

That last line is the whole point: the revision came back from the app's own event stream, so "it reloaded" is a fact, not a hope.

A plugin the running app never loaded cannot be reloaded, and the app says so by leaving it out of the graph it sends first. `dev` reads that graph, so a freshly installed plugin gets the sentence that fixes it instead of a timeout:

```
copied, but not confirmed: the running app has not loaded demo-panel, so it will not report a reload; restart the app once after installing it
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dest <dir>` | write into this installed copy instead of searching `~/.dsh/profiles/*/node_modules/<name>` |
| `--entry <file>` | copy this file instead of `dsh.client.entry`, `client.js`, `lib/client.js` |
| `--build <command>` | run this before each copy (a failed build copies nothing) |
| `--host <url>` | confirm the reload against the app at this URL; without it the copy still happens and the tool says it is unconfirmed |
| `--once` | copy once and exit, for scripts |

Two things it does not do, because the host does not: React state inside the reloaded plugin is lost, and a failed swap does not roll back to the previous bundle.

## Use it in CI

The same checks run as a GitHub Action, so a tag cannot go out on a plugin that would not install:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit@v1
  with:
    dir: plugin        # the folder holding the plugin's package.json
    command: verify    # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
```

`verify` is the default because it is the only check that reads what a user
actually installs: `doctor` reads the working copy, so a `files` list that
forgets `client.js` passes it and fails only after `npm i`.

`command: doctor` stops at the manifest checks (fast, no install), and
`command: index` audits `market/index.json` instead, failing on any version that
cannot state a host range. Pin `version:` if you would rather not track the
latest release.

## Check a plugin you have not cloned

The panel takes three kinds of input: a folder, `owner/repo`, or a GitHub URL.
A bare name is a search, not a guess — it asks GitHub, lists the matches with
their stars, and checks the one you pick. A repository is downloaded once as a
tarball into a temp folder, so nothing is cloned into your workspace and
nothing is installed.

The CLI reads a repository straight from the GitHub API:

```bash
dsh-plugin doctor --remote V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
```

```text
dsh-plugin doctor: 1 problem(s) in V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
  ⨯ engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"; declare the range you support, e.g. "engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.0" }
```

That is the whole reason this mode exists: the plugin hub files failed installs
back into plugin repositories, and the report is a sentence — `plugin install
failed`, `plugin does not support the DSH version in use` — that never names a
file. Reading `package.json` over the API is enough to name it.

What it can see, and what it cannot:

- Manifest checks (`engines.dsh`, `files`, `dsh.client`, `exports`) run on the
  real `package.json`.
- File checks (does `exports["./client"]` point at a file that exists, does the
  root export `apply`) need the tree. A package that runs `prepack`,
  `prepublishOnly`, `prepare` or `build` publishes files it does not commit, so
  those checks are **skipped with a note** instead of calling a working plugin
  broken.
- Public repositories work anonymously, but GitHub allows 60 requests an hour.
  Export `GH_TOKEN` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) to audit more than one or two.

To check a whole list in one pass, put one `owner/repo` per line in a file and
pass it with `--from` (`-` reads standard input):

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt
```

Repositories are read four at a time by default. `--jobs N` changes that width;
values above `8` are capped at `8`, and `--jobs 1` walks the list one repository
at a time, the timing the command had before batching. The output — and the
`--json` array — still follows the input list, and every verdict is the one the
sequential run produced, so a diff between two runs compares repositories rather
than scheduling.

When GitHub answers `403` or `429`, the shared quota is gone, so the batch stops
starting new repositories and marks every entry it could not read as
`rate-limited` instead of `clean` or `unreadable`. If the response carries
`x-ratelimit-reset` (or `retry-after`), the reset time is printed with the
verdict, and the remaining entries are reported without another request.

### Will this plugin install on my DSH?

The seven compatibility reports all end with the same question. Add `--host
<version>` to a remote audit and it answers that question for one repository.
This is a real run against `L3n3L/dsh-resume`, a plugin whose declared range
stops before DSH 0.2.0, checked against the `0.2.2-alpha.3` canary from the
reports:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
incompatible  L3n3L/dsh-resume  0.1.3 (host >=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0) [incompatible with dsh 0.2.2-alpha.3; declares ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"]

summary: 1 repository — 0 clean, 1 failing (1 problem), 0 unreadable, 0 rate-limited
```

The verdict comes first: `incompatible` means the range in `package.json` does
not accept the host, so the installer rejects the plugin before it unpacks it.
This run exits `1`. The same answer is reproducible without a GitHub request —
the manifest is checked in under `examples/compatibility-sample/`, and this
command feeds it through the real CLI path:

```sh
$ node scripts/compatibility-sample.mjs
```

(`npm run compatibility` runs the same script.) The test suite runs that
command and compares its output with the block above, so the sample cannot
drift from the formatter or from the README.

The line carries the range `package.json` declares and one of `compatible`,
`incompatible`, or `unknown` against that host version. `unknown` is the honest
answer for a missing or malformed range — there is nothing to compare — while a
range that excludes the host is `incompatible`, counted as failing, and exits
`1`. The same flag works in the batch mode, so one `--from` run answers the
whole list:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
```

The compatibility flags are `--remote <owner/repo>` for one repository,
`--from <file>` for a list (`-` reads standard input), `--host <version>` for
the DSH version to compare against, and `--json` for the machine-readable
finding. `--jobs <n>` sets the batch width, and `--patch-dir <dir>` writes the
host-targeted repair for each repository that needs one. The help text lists
the same flags; a test fails if this section names a flag the CLI does not have.

`--host` still names the running app URL for a local `audit`; on `--remote` it
is the DSH version to compare against. With `--json`, each finding gains
`host` and `compatibility` beside `hostRange`.

Each repository gets one line with its verdict — `clean`, `failing`,
`unreadable`, or `rate-limited` — and the run ends with a counted summary:

```text
clean         demo/plugin  1.2.3 (host >=0.2.0)
failing       demo/broken  — engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"
rate-limited  demo/blocked — GitHub rate-limited this request (403) for package.json; set GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN to raise the limit; the limit resets at 2026-11-04T20:00:00.000Z
rate-limited  demo/next    — GitHub rate-limited the batch before this repository was read, so it was not requested; the limit resets at 2026-11-04T20:00:00.000Z

summary: 4 repositories — 1 clean, 1 failing (1 problem), 0 unreadable, 2 rate-limited
```

The command exits `1` when any repository is failing, unreadable, or
rate-limited, and `0` only when every repository in the list is clean. `--from`
also accepts the JSON evidence shape (an array, or an object with `rows`) that
the old shell loop printed, so an existing audit file can be replayed without
rewriting it.

### Measured throughput

The measurement uses the first eight repositories from the 3 November
install-failure list — `610la/dsh-notification-center`,
`Anionex/dsh-vision-toolkit`, `ChongCyrus/Vibe-Mathematics`,
`CrazyShout/dsh-ssh-remote`, `Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model`,
`FSMargoo/dsh-at-file`, `FylarOpen/dsh-fylar-office-editor` and
`GraySilver/dsh-evolve-modes` — served from memory with a fixed 500 ms delay on
every API request. That makes the number reproducible on any host: it measures
the batch's scheduling, not GitHub's mood. Reproduce it with:

```sh
$ npm run benchmark
```

(`node scripts/benchmark-audit.mjs` runs the same harness without npm's banner.)
The tarball ships both that script and the list it reads, so the command runs in
a checkout and in an installed copy. The test suite packs the package, installs
the tarball into a temp directory and runs the documented command there;
[`docs/benchmark-tarball.md`](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/blob/main/docs/benchmark-tarball.md)
records the packaging gap this closes.

It runs the same list twice: `--jobs 1`, which is the loop the command used
before batching, and the default `--jobs 4`. Measured on this host:

| run | wall clock | seconds per repository |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before (`--jobs 1`) | 8.03 s | 1.003 s |
| after (default `--jobs 4`) | 2.01 s | 0.251 s |

The after run keeps four reads in flight, so eight repositories finish in two
waves and the per-repository cost falls from about 1.00 s to about 0.25 s. The
test suite reads this table and fails if the after number no longer matches the
default `--jobs` value, so changing the default cannot leave the claim behind.

For a CI job or a repair sweep, add `--json`:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt --json
```
[
  {
    "target": "V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions",
    "version": "0.3.0",
    "hostRange": ">=0.2.0",
    "failures": [],
    "notes": []
  },
  {
    "target": "demo/plugin",
    "version": "1.2.3",
    "hostRange": null,
    "failures": [
      {
        "check": "engines.dsh",
        "message": "engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as \"incompatible with dsh\"; declare the range you support, e.g. \"engines\": { \"dsh\": \">=0.2.0\" }"
      }
    ],
    "notes": []
  }
]
```

Every repository produces one object with `target`, `version`, `hostRange`,
`failures` (`{ check, message }`) and `notes`, and the command exits `1` when any
repository has a problem. With `--host <version>` each object also carries
`host` and `compatibility`. A rate-limited repository adds `rateLimited: true`
and a `rateLimit` object with the HTTP `status` and, when GitHub sent one,
`resetAt`; it is not marked `unreadable`. A network error is printed in `notes`
and still exits `1`: a repository the tool could not read is never reported as
clean. Packages that build before they pack
keep their file-level checks in `notes` as before.

When the list is a repair queue rather than a report, add `--patch-dir`:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt --patch-dir repairs/
```

It creates the directory and writes one `owner__repo.patch` for every
repository whose `engines.dsh` check fails, with the same diff `fix --remote
--patch` produces. Repositories that are clean, unreadable, or need a repair
the tool cannot make automatically are skipped. The repository itself is still
only read, and `--force` replaces a patch that is already there.

### The 3 November list

The install-failure audit that started this tool covers 67 repositories. Its
list is checked in as
[`docs/ecosystem-audit-2026-11-03.txt`](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/blob/main/docs/ecosystem-audit-2026-11-03.txt),
one `owner/repo` per line. One command audits all of it and leaves the repairs
in `/tmp/repairs`:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from docs/ecosystem-audit-2026-11-03.txt --patch-dir /tmp/repairs
```

A real run. The rows in the middle are elided; the summary is exactly what the
command printed:

```text
failing     610la/dsh-notification-center  — engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a

decision.reason: The frozen manifest is an example, fixture, template, evaluation support package, rollback copy, or archive rather than a catalog entry.
